authors: Rama Cont; Arseniy Kukanov; Sasha Stoikov
title: The Price Impact of Order Book Events
geography_market: 50 randomly selected S&P 500 stocks on U.S. consolidated markets
target: Contemporaneous short-interval mid-price change and intraday volatility
horizon: H1—short intraday buckets, contemporaneous rather than forward
predictor_family: Best-quote order-flow imbalance, depth, trades, limit orders, and cancellations
model_family: Linear impact regression and scaling analysis
sample_design: NYSE TAQ trades and Level-1 consolidated quotes for one calendar month, April 2010, across 50 stocks; robustness checks span stocks, time scales, and intraday seasonality.
benchmark: Signed trade volume and depth-only impact relations
pit_status: NOT-APPLICABLE — OFI and price changes are measured over the same interval
native_result: Association result: price changes are approximately linear in contemporaneous OFI, with slope inversely related to depth, and this relation is more robust than volume impact. Forecast accuracy and trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: Discusses adverse selection and depth but does not test an executable forecast, spread crossing, latency, impact, or capacity.
replication_decay: OFI becomes a core input in later chronological LOB forecasts, but this study itself is not forward-predictive evidence.
openness: Open arXiv version; TAQ data require a WRDS license.
key_limitation: Contemporaneous construction is fatal if interpreted as a forecast, and timestamps are rounded to one second.

authors: Martin D. Gould; Julius Bonart
title: Queue Imbalance as a One-Tick-Ahead Price Predictor in a Limit Order Book
target: Direction and probability of the next mid-price movement
predictor_family: Best-bid/best-ask queue imbalance
model_family: Logistic and local-logistic classification
sample_design: LOBSTER observations from 2014; each stock's time series is randomly partitioned 80/20 into 20,160 training and 5,040 test observations, with five-fold tuning inside training.
benchmark: Unconditional 50/50 next-direction null
pit_status: NOT-APPLICABLE — features precede labels, but train and test observations are randomly interleaved through time
native_result: Reported accuracy: test AUC is about 0.70-0.80 for large-tick stocks and 0.60-0.65 for small-tick stocks; probability MSE improves 20%-30% and 2%-6%, respectively. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No spread, fill, latency, impact, or capacity model; local logistic fitting is more computationally expensive.
replication_decay: Later chronological studies support queue/order-flow signal at very short horizons, but this paper's random split does not qualify as held-out time-series evidence.
openness: Open manuscript; LOBSTER data are licensed.
key_limitation: Random train/test splitting violates the protocol for dependent time-series targets and can leak regimes across sets.

authors: Matteo Aquilina; Eric Budish; Peter O'Neill
title: Quantifying the High-Frequency Trading Arms Race
target: Latency-race incidence, duration, profit, and contribution to liquidity cost
predictor_family: Complete exchange messages, including failed trade and cancel attempts
model_family: Race-detection algorithm, spread decomposition, and economic extrapolation
sample_design: All LSE messages for FTSE 350 stocks over nine weeks in fall 2015, timestamped at the exchange network edge with microsecond accuracy; extensive race-definition sensitivity checks.
benchmark: Conventional order-book data, effective spreads, and price-impact decompositions that cannot observe race losers
pit_status: NOT-APPLICABLE — direct measurement of realized market races rather than a forecast
native_result: Market-cost result: about 537 races per FTSE 100 symbol-day, modal duration 5-10 microseconds, roughly 22% of FTSE 100 volume in races, 0.42-bp tax on total volume, and 17% implied liquidity-cost reduction if races were eliminated.
costs_capacity: Directly measures realized race profits and liquidity costs; top six firms account for more than 80% of wins and losses. Global $5 billion annual stakes are an extrapolation, not audited P&L.
replication_decay: Uses regulator-obtained message data unavailable in ordinary LOB studies; comparable public independent datasets remain rare.
openness: Open BIS paper and published article; participant-level exchange messages are confidential.
key_limitation: Nine weeks in one 2015 equity venue support precise local estimates but not the global extrapolation or other asset classes.

authors: Matteo Prata; Giuseppe Masi; Leonardo Berti; Viviana Arrigoni; Andrea Coletta; Irene Cannistraci; Svitlana Vyetrenko; Paola Velardi; Novella Bartolini
title: LOB-Based Deep Learning Models for Stock Price Trend Prediction: A Benchmark Study
geography_market: Nasdaq Nordic FI-2010 and six Nasdaq stocks in LOB-2021/LOB-2022
target: Three-class mid-price trend
predictor_family: Ten-level limit order books
model_family: Thirteen published deep networks, MLP/LSTM baselines, ensembles, and tree models
sample_design: Reimplements fifteen models on FI-2010 and externally tests them on six LOBSTER stocks over July 1-15, 2021 and February 1-15, 2022 using five random seeds and new hyperparameter searches.
benchmark: Published FI-2010 scores, MLP, LSTM, and classical tree ensembles
pit_status: PIT—chronological LOB datasets are separated by market and era; tuning uses validation data
native_result: Forecast accuracy: all models suffer significant performance deterioration on new LOB data despite stronger FI-2010 scores. P&L: only NFLX and LSTR are profitable in the paper's simulation, largely tracking underlying drift.
costs_capacity: Simulation executes at mid-price and ignores transaction costs, impact, position sizing, and capacity; several deep models have millisecond inference times that may be unsuitable for HFT.
replication_decay: Independent reimplementation directly weakens the external-validity claims of the FI-2010 deep-LOB lineage.
openness: Open-access paper and open-source LOBCAST framework; FI-2010 is public and LOBSTER test data are licensed.
key_limitation: The external samples are only ten days each, but their adverse result is strengthened by cross-model consistency.

authors: Hendrik Bessembinder
title: Systematic Risk, Hedging Pressure, and Risk Premiums in Futures Markets
geography_market: U.S. agricultural, foreign-currency, and other futures markets
target: Futures excess return, not cash spot return
predictor_family: Own-market net hedger positions and systematic risk
model_family: Cross-sectional asset-pricing regressions
sample_design: Historical futures returns and hedger-position measures across asset groups with systematic-risk controls
benchmark: Integrated futures/asset-market risk-pricing model without hedging pressure
pit_status: PARTIAL — position data are dated, but publication lags and exact trade timing are not modeled as an executable signal
native_result: Foreign-currency and agricultural futures returns varied with hedgers' net holdings after controlling for systematic risk.
costs_capacity: No portfolio turnover, bid-ask, margin, impact, or capacity evaluation.
replication_decay: de Roon, Nijman, and Veld (2000) found related own/cross-market effects, while Gorton, Hayashi, and Rouwenhorst (2013) found no subsequent-return prediction from participant positions.
openness: Publisher metadata are public; no verified open replication package.
key_limitation: In-sample cross-sectional pricing and coarse position data do not establish a point-in-time, cost-adjusted profitable hedging-pressure strategy.

authors: Eugene F. Fama; Kenneth R. French
title: Commodity Futures Prices: Some Evidence on Forecast Power, Premiums, and the Theory of Storage
target: Cash spot price at futures maturity and futures premium; cash spot is not treated as a rolled futures return
predictor_family: Futures basis, interest rates, storage costs, convenience yield, and seasonals
model_family: Theory-of-storage regressions and futures-price forecast decompositions
sample_design: Commodity-by-commodity historical regressions separating maturity-spot forecasts from expected futures premiums
benchmark: Current cash spot price and constant-premium/no-forecast-power restrictions
pit_status: PIT — for quoted cash/futures prices; storage and convenience yield are partly latent
native_result: Futures prices had maturity-spot forecast power for 10 of 21 commodities, while five showed time-varying expected premiums; basis also varied with rates and seasonal convenience yields.
costs_capacity: Price-forecast study; no rolled-contract costs, collateral return, impact, or capacity analysis.
replication_decay: Later inventory/basis research supports storage links but shows large commodity and era heterogeneity.
openness: Stable DOI/RePEc metadata are public; no verified original code/data package.
key_limitation: Forecast power for future cash spot and a futures risk premium are jointly identified only through maintained decomposition assumptions.

authors: Gary B. Gorton; K. Geert Rouwenhorst
title: Facts and Fantasies about Commodity Futures
geography_market: Diversified U.S. and London commodity futures
target: Fully collateralized rolled-futures total return and futures excess return, explicitly not cash spot return
horizon: H3-H6; monthly returns summarized over July 1959-December 2004
predictor_family: Long-only futures risk premium, business cycle, and inflation exposure
model_family: Equally weighted collateralized index and descriptive risk-premium analysis
sample_design: Historical monthly index assembled from individual futures with systematic rolling and collateral
benchmark: U.S. equities, bonds, T-bills, inflation, and an uncollateralized spot-price interpretation
pit_status: PIT — for futures prices and stated roll rule; historical contract-universe reconstruction is not fully audited here
native_result: The collateralized index earned about a 5% annual excess return with an equity-like Sharpe ratio and negative stock/bond correlation.
costs_capacity: Rolls and collateral are included conceptually, but bid-ask, commissions, impact, margin financing, and capacity are not fully deducted.
replication_decay: Post-2004 long-only commodity performance has been materially weaker and regime-dependent; the original estimate is not a prospective forecast.
openness: Public NBER/manuscript versions and construction discussion are available; no verified turnkey index code.
key_limitation: A historical average risk premium is not return predictability, and the result is sensitive to sample, weighting, collateral, and roll conventions.

authors: Joëlle Miffre; Georgios Rallis
title: Momentum Strategies in Commodity Futures Markets
geography_market: Thirty-one U.S. agricultural, livestock, metal, and energy futures
target: Rolled nearby commodity-futures long-short return, not cash spot return
predictor_family: Cross-sectional momentum and long-horizon reversal
model_family: Winner-minus-loser portfolio sorts
sample_design: Historical settlement-price backtest over 31 contracts and a broad formation/holding grid
benchmark: Contrarian portfolios, traditional assets, and zero abnormal futures return
pit_status: PIT — signals use lagged settlement prices and nearby liquid contracts
native_result: Thirteen momentum variants were profitable with about 9.38% average annual return; contrarian rules failed, and winners tended to be backwardated while losers were contangoed.
costs_capacity: Liquidity and low futures costs are argued rather than measured with realized fills; roll, impact, and capacity are incomplete.
replication_decay: Fuertes, Miffre, and Rallis (2010) extended the signal with curve information; later multiple-testing work weakens broad time-series momentum claims.
openness: Public SSRN record and publisher metadata are available; no verified complete replication code.
key_limitation: Thirteen winners emerge from a large strategy grid without a sealed test, and momentum overlaps economically with the futures curve.

authors: Ana-Maria Fuertes; Joëlle Miffre; Georgios Rallis
title: Tactical Allocation in Commodity Futures Markets: Combining Momentum and Term Structure Signals
target: Long-short rolled-futures return, not cash spot return
horizon: H3-H4; monthly rebalancing with 1-12 month momentum windows
predictor_family: Cross-sectional momentum plus futures-curve term structure
model_family: Single- and double-sort portfolio backtests
sample_design: January 1979-September 2004 historical backtest with liquidity screens, alternative roll-yield definitions, and robustness checks
benchmark: Momentum-only, term-structure-only, equally weighted commodities, and traditional assets
pit_status: PIT — lagged returns and contemporaneous futures curves are observable at formation
native_result: Momentum and curve strategies earned 10.14% and 12.66% annualized alpha; the combined strategy earned 21.02% gross and 20.41% after modeled costs.
costs_capacity: Round-trip costs and turnover were modeled; realized slippage, nonlinear impact, roll crowding, and institutional capacity were not.
replication_decay: Later factor studies retain momentum and basis signals, but the exact double sort lacks a sealed independent holdout.
openness: Public accepted manuscript and publisher metadata are available; no verified turnkey code/data archive.
key_limitation: The same historical sample was used to compare many signal definitions and combinations, so the very large alpha is vulnerable to selection.

authors: Hossein Rad; Rand Kwong Yew Low; Joëlle Miffre; Robert W. Faff
title: The Commodity Risk Premium and Neural Networks
target: Next-month commodity-futures risk premium and portfolio excess return, not cash spot return
predictor_family: One hundred twenty-eight macroeconomic and financial predictors
model_family: Equal-weight shrinkage, principal components, feedforward DNN, and LSTM-DNN
sample_design: January 1979-December 1999 training sample and January 2000-December 2019 untouched chronological test sample
benchmark: Linear shrinkage models and previously documented commodity factors
pit_status: PARTIAL — strict chronological split, but macro predictors are not documented as real-time vintage series
native_result: LSTM-DNN is the strongest specification; its test-period portfolio retains about 5.75% significant annual excess return after an 8.6 bp round-trip cost under the paper's assumptions.
costs_capacity: Applies 8.6 bp round-trip costs and illiquidity checks; nonlinear impact, margin funding, model operations, and capacity are not audited.
replication_decay: The two-decade holdout is substantial, but no independent team or post-publication external-period replication was located.
openness: Public SSRN/postprint and publisher metadata are available; no verified executable training/data package.
key_limitation: High-dimensional architecture and predictor preprocessing remain difficult to audit, and revised macro data may overstate real-time feasibility.

authors: Shirui Wang; Tianyang Zhang
title: Predictability of Commodity Futures Returns with Machine Learning Models
geography_market: Twenty-two agriculture, livestock, metal, and energy futures
target: Next-month individual commodity-futures return and long-short portfolio return, not cash spot return
predictor_family: Commodity-specific and macro-financial characteristics
model_family: Elastic net, PCR, SVR, LightGBM, neural network, and Shapley attribution
sample_design: May 1997-December 2018 chronological 70% train/20% validation/10% test split; test begins October 2016
benchmark: AR(1) and forecast-combination models
pit_status: PARTIAL — chronological split and lagged features, but macro data vintages are not reconstructed
native_result: LightGBM had the lowest average test MSE and significantly beat both benchmarks; its top-five/bottom-five portfolio reported 35% annualized return and a 2.07 Sharpe ratio after a 0.1% assumed cost.
costs_capacity: A flat 0.1% opening/closing cost was imposed; roll mechanics, liquidity variation, nonlinear impact, and capacity were not modeled.
replication_decay: No independent replication or post-publication external-period test was located by the cutoff.
openness: The article is publicly accessible with detailed method/results; no verified full code/data archive.
key_limitation: The test window is only about 27 months, and LightGBM was selected as the winner using test errors before its portfolio performance was highlighted.

authors: Yan Li; Qingfu Liu; Deyu Miao; Yiuman Tse
title: Return Seasonality in Commodity Futures
target: Monthly commodity-futures return and seasonality-strategy return, not cash spot return
predictor_family: Same-calendar-month, half-month, and annual return seasonality; momentum/reversal combinations
model_family: Calendar portfolio backtests and rolling/subperiod comparisons
sample_design: Monthly 1970-October 2023 data with overlapping long subperiods and explicit recent-period tests
benchmark: Other-month returns, momentum, reversal, and combined strategies
pit_status: PIT — calendar and lagged-return signals are known at formation
native_result: Standalone seasonality appeared in only a few early commodities, concentrated around 1990-1999, and was insignificant in 2004-2023; some combined momentum/reversal-seasonality returns remained positive.
costs_capacity: No comprehensive realized spread, roll-impact, or capacity analysis for the composite strategy.
replication_decay: Directly extends earlier same-month seasonality through 2023 and documents substantial post-publication decay.
openness: Publisher metadata and an SSRN version are public; no verified code/data package.
key_limitation: The recent null is not a formal equivalence bound, while overlapping subperiods and newly tried combinations still permit selection.

authors: Gary B. Gorton; Fumio Hayashi; K. Geert Rouwenhorst
title: The Fundamentals of Commodity Futures Returns
geography_market: Thirty-one commodity futures with participant-position data
target: Subsequent commodity-futures excess return, not contemporaneous price or cash spot return
predictor_family: Commercial/speculative positions and hedging pressure
model_family: Predictive regressions conditional on inventory and price signals
sample_design: 1971-2010 futures/inventory study with a separate participant-position return-prediction claim
benchmark: Inventory/basis signals and no predictive relation from participant positions
pit_status: PARTIAL — positions are dated but reporting availability is not modeled at executable granularity
native_result: Participant positions were contemporaneously related to inventories and prices but showed no evidence of predicting subsequent futures returns.
costs_capacity: No strategy-cost analysis is needed for the null; power against small net effects is not expressed as an equivalence bound.
replication_decay: This conflicts with earlier Bessembinder and de Roon hedging-pressure results, leaving material design and sample heterogeneity.
openness: Public NBER and author manuscripts are available; no verified complete replication package.
key_limitation: The null is not a formal equivalence result, and aggregation, reporting lag, trader classification, and inventory controls differ from earlier studies.

authors: Marta Szymanowska; Frans A. de Roon; Theo E. Nijman; Rob van den Goorbergh
title: An Anatomy of Commodity Futures Risk Premia
geography_market: Twenty-one liquid commodity futures across seven sectors
target: Futures spot-premium and term-premium components; 'spot premium' is a futures-return decomposition, not a cash spot return
horizon: H3-H4; bimonthly returns across 2-8 month maturities
predictor_family: Basis, momentum, volatility, inflation, hedging pressure, and liquidity
model_family: Characteristic sorts, return decomposition, and factor pricing
sample_design: March 1986-December 2010 CRB futures panel with multiple maturities and sector controls
benchmark: Unconditional futures returns and alternative commodity characteristics
pit_status: PIT — for market characteristics; position/liquidity publication timing is less complete
native_result: Characteristic sorts generated 5%-14% annual spot premia and 1%-3% term premia; one basis factor explained spot premia and two more explained term premia.
costs_capacity: No full realized-cost, roll-impact, margin, or capacity analysis for all sorts.
replication_decay: Boons and Prado (2019) added basis-momentum, but no locked prospective test validates the selected factor set.
openness: Public SSRN record and repository metadata are available; no verified full replication code.
key_limitation: Many characteristics and internally constructed factors are tested in-sample, so explanatory fit is not independent forecast evidence.

authors: Martijn Boons; Melissa Porras Prado
title: Basis-Momentum
target: Future futures spot- and term-premium components, not cash spot return
horizon: H3-H4; short-horizon returns across futures maturities
predictor_family: Basis-momentum from changes in futures-curve slope and curvature
model_family: Time-series and cross-sectional predictive regressions, portfolio sorts, and factor pricing
sample_design: Historical commodity panel with benchmark characteristics, individual commodities, sorted portfolios, and robustness tests
benchmark: Static basis, momentum, storage/inventory, and hedging-pressure explanations
pit_status: PIT — futures-curve prices needed for the signal are contemporaneously observable
native_result: Basis-momentum strongly outperformed benchmark characteristics in predicting both futures spot and term premia and was priced across portfolios and individual commodities.
costs_capacity: Implementation frictions and curve liquidity were not validated with live fills or nonlinear impact.
replication_decay: Published supplementary data improve reproducibility, but no independent sealed or prospective replication is established.
openness: Publisher page identifies supplementary replication data and a public manuscript is available.
key_limitation: The signal and risk interpretation were developed and tested on the same historical panel, with limited external-period evidence.

authors: Tobias J. Moskowitz; Yao Hua Ooi; Lasse Heje Pedersen
title: Time Series Momentum
geography_market: Twenty-four commodities, 12 currency crosses, nine equity indexes, and 13 government-bond futures
target: Next-month futures/forward excess return; commodity futures and FX forwards are not cash spot returns
horizon: H3; past 1-12 months predicting the next month
predictor_family: Own-return time-series momentum/trend
model_family: Asset-level predictive regressions and volatility-scaled sign portfolios
sample_design: Fifty-eight liquid instruments, January 1965-December 2009, with asset-class and subperiod robustness
benchmark: Standard asset-pricing factors, buy-and-hold, and no return autocovariance
pit_status: PIT — signals use lagged liquid futures and forward returns
native_result: Past 12-month return positively predicted next-month return across all four asset classes; the diversified strategy had substantial abnormal returns and crisis convexity.
costs_capacity: Liquid instruments were selected and turnover discussed, but original headline returns do not contain a complete realized-cost/impact/capacity audit.
replication_decay: Huang et al. (2020) reanalyzed the same 55-instrument core and found weak asset-level and out-of-sample evidence after corrected inference.
openness: Original monthly factor data are publicly downloadable; public manuscript is available.
key_limitation: Pooled inference, volatility scaling, and a net long component can make portfolio profitability look like predictability even when asset-level slopes are weak.

authors: Zihao Zhang; Stefan Zohren; Stephen Roberts
title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Trading
venue: The Journal of Financial Data Science 2(2): 25-40
asset_class: Commodity, equity-index, fixed-income, and currency futures
target: Daily position and risk-adjusted trading return
predictor_family: Lagged normalized returns and technical state variables
model_family: Deep reinforcement learning with DQN, policy-gradient, and actor-critic variants
sample_design: Fifty continuous futures from 2011-2019 with chronological train, validation, and out-of-sample tests
benchmark: Long-only, time-series momentum, and standard rule-based strategies
pit_status: PARTIAL — Signals are lagged and splits chronological; continuous-contract construction and vendor histories are not fully point-in-time auditable
native_result: Policy-gradient methods improve out-of-sample risk-adjusted returns over momentum and other DRL variants across the broad futures set
costs_capacity: Commissions and bid-ask spread assumptions are included, including heavy-cost scenarios; nonlinear impact, margin financing, and crowded capacity are omitted
replication_decay: Cross-asset breadth supports within-study external validity, but no independent team or live execution record verifies the magnitude
openness: Paper and preprint are public; full licensed futures history and an archival end-to-end pipeline are not guaranteed
key_limitation: Retrospective hyperparameter selection across many markets can still exploit common regimes, and linear costs favor scalable futures assumptions

authors: Pierre Collin-Dufresne; Robert S. Goldstein; J. Spencer Martin
title: The Determinants of Credit Spread Changes
target: Monthly corporate credit-spread changes
predictor_family: Structural credit, macro, equity, and liquidity variables
model_family: Panel regressions and principal components
sample_design: 688 noncallable industrial bonds from 261 issuers, July 1988-December 1997
benchmark: Structural-model determinants and standard liquidity proxies
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Primarily contemporaneous explanation, not a genuine forecast-origin design
native_result: Theory variables explain at most about 25% of spread changes; residuals share a dominant unidentified common factor
costs_capacity: No trade, bid-ask, impact, or capacity assessment
replication_decay: Avramov-Jostova-Philipov and CDS evidence find more fundamental explanatory power in other samples
openness: DOI, SSRN, and public manuscript; dealer quote data proprietary
key_limitation: Contemporaneous regressions cannot establish forecastability and the sample predates TRACE

authors: William R. Gebhardt; Soeren Hvidkjaer; Bhaskaran Swaminathan
title: Stock and Bond Market Interaction: Does Momentum Spill Over?
target: Subsequent corporate-bond returns and rating changes
horizon: H4; prior 12 months to next 12 months
predictor_family: Cross-asset equity momentum
model_family: Portfolio sorts and predictive regressions
sample_design: NYSE/AMEX/Nasdaq issuers with Lehman bond prices, January 1973-December 1996
benchmark: Own-bond momentum, risk, liquidity, infrequent trading, and earnings-surprise controls
pit_status: PARTIAL — Prior equity returns precede bond outcomes; month-end quote histories and filters are retrospective
native_result: Investment-grade bonds reverse on own past returns, but issuer equity momentum predicts next-year bond returns and ratings
costs_capacity: Basic transaction-cost and infrequent-trading checks; impact and shortability are absent
replication_decay: Jostova finds own-bond momentum only in non-investment-grade debt, confirming grade heterogeneity
openness: DOI and SSRN metadata public; Lehman bond data proprietary
key_limitation: Old quote-based sample, no chronological holdout, and difficult short-side implementation

authors: Robin Greenwood; Samuel G. Hanson
title: Issuer Quality and Corporate Bond Returns
target: Cumulative excess corporate-bond returns
predictor_family: Issuance quality and credit-cycle composition
model_family: Time-series predictive regressions
sample_design: Ratings issuance history, 1926-2008; EDF-based quality measure, 1962-2008
benchmark: Aggregate credit growth, debt issuance quantity, and term spread
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Issuance composition is dated; EDF history and coefficients are assembled retrospectively
native_result: Poor issuer quality predicts low returns; one-SD deterioration lowers next-year HY excess return about 4.5%, with R-squared 12%
costs_capacity: Long-horizon index returns; turnover is low but spreads, defaults, taxes, and capacity are not modeled
replication_decay: Related credit-cycle work supports issuance composition, but no locked prospective strategy is public
openness: DOI and author manuscript public; EDF inputs proprietary
key_limitation: Overlapping long-horizon regressions and few independent credit cycles

authors: Gergana Jostova; Stanislava Nikolova; Alexander Philipov; Christof W. Stahel
title: Momentum in Corporate Bond Returns
target: Monthly corporate-bond returns
horizon: H3; six-month formation and monthly holding
predictor_family: Bond momentum
model_family: Credit-stratified portfolio sorts
sample_design: 81,491 bonds and 3.75 million bond-months across quote and trade databases, 1973-2011
benchmark: Risk factors, equity momentum, illiquidity, opaqueness, and transaction costs
pit_status: PARTIAL — Lagged returns are observable; bond survival, sparse prices, and ex-post return filters threaten PIT construction
native_result: 1991-2011 momentum averages 192 bps monthly in non-investment-grade bonds but is absent in investment grade
costs_capacity: Reported profits exceed TRACE-based modeled costs; nonlinear impact, delay, and short availability are not modeled
replication_decay: The 2026 open replication finds six- and twelve-month momentum highly sensitive to price error and ex-post filtering
openness: DOI and FDIC working paper public; several underlying databases proprietary
key_limitation: Effect is concentrated in distressed, illiquid bonds where feasible return measurement and shorting are hardest

authors: Patrick Houweling; Jeroen van Zundert
title: Factor Investing in the Corporate Bond Market
geography_market: United States investment-grade and high-yield bonds
target: Monthly factor returns, alpha, and information ratio
predictor_family: Size, low-risk, value, and momentum
model_family: Single- and multifactor portfolio sorts
sample_design: Barclays index constituents, January 1994-December 2013; over 1.1 million bond-months
benchmark: Corporate-bond market index and bond/equity factor models
pit_status: PARTIAL — Monthly characteristics and constituents are lagged; no sealed test and index-history construction is proprietary
native_result: Four factors have significant alphas; the cost-adjusted multifactor Sharpe under the paper's modeled transaction costs falls to 0.26 in investment grade and 0.46 in high yield but remains above the market.
costs_capacity: Applies modeled transaction costs and liquid-bond checks; nonlinear impact, delays, and capacity are absent
replication_decay: Dickerson-Mueller-Robotti and the 2026 factor-zoo replication challenge most incremental factor premia
openness: DOI, CFA summary, and working paper public; constituent data licensed
key_limitation: Practitioner-designed factors are evaluated in one proprietary historical universe

authors: Jennie Bai; Turan G. Bali; Quan Wen
title: Common Risk Factors in the Cross-Section of Corporate Bond Returns (Retracted)
venue: Journal of Financial Economics 131: 619-642; retracted 2023 with official notice
target: Monthly factor returns and cross-sectional pricing
predictor_family: Downside, credit, and liquidity risk
model_family: Portfolio factors and cross-sectional asset pricing
sample_design: Original public factors cover August 2004-December 2016; independently reconstructed after publication
benchmark: Corporate-bond market factor
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Fatal lead/lag temporal misalignment; original factor returns included future-month information
native_result: Authors confirmed the main factor-pricing result does not survive correction; article was formally retracted
costs_capacity: Original gross factor results are moot; costs would not repair the timing error
replication_decay: Independent replication identified the error; publisher retraction supersedes the original affirmative claim
openness: Official public retraction notice and corrected replication materials available
key_limitation: Invalid temporal alignment and asymmetric data handling; the 2019 article was formally retracted in 2023.

authors: Bryan Kelly; Diogo Palhares; Seth Pruitt
title: Modeling Corporate Bond Returns
target: Next-month returns, pricing errors, and systematic portfolio returns
predictor_family: Bond characteristics and debt-equity cross-asset factors
model_family: Instrumented principal components conditional factor model
sample_design: ICE bond data, December 1999-December 2020; 14,600 bonds and 555,894 bond-months
benchmark: Bond CAPM, Fama-French, Bai-Bali-Wen, and characteristic models
pit_status: PARTIAL — Characteristics are lagged and OOS windows chronological; proprietary analytics limit timestamp audit
native_result: The expected-return quintile strategy has OOS Sharpe 3.5 gross and 1.4 after the paper's fixed 19-bp one-way cost assumption.
costs_capacity: Uses 19 bps per one-way trade; no nonlinear size impact, execution delay, borrow, or capacity
replication_decay: The very large cost-adjusted Sharpe under a fixed-cost model lacks independent fresh-data replication and faces the broader 2026 factor-replication critique.
openness: DOI and manuscript public; ICE data and analytics proprietary
key_limitation: Fixed costs and frictionless long-short execution are optimistic for an OTC bond strategy

authors: Alexander Dickerson; Philippe Mueller; Cesare Robotti
title: Priced Risk in Corporate Bonds
geography_market: United States corporate bonds across multiple databases
target: Incremental factor pricing and expected excess returns
predictor_family: Credit, downside, liquidity, and other traded/nontraded factors
model_family: Identification-robust factor and model-comparison tests
sample_design: Independent portfolio- and bond-level reconstructions, emphasizing the 2004-2016 Bai-Bali-Wen window
benchmark: Single corporate-bond market factor
pit_status: PIT — Corrects lead/lag errors and compares properly aligned factor series
native_result: Previously proposed factors add no robust pricing power beyond the bond market, with traded liquidity only a marginal exception
costs_capacity: Main tests are gross; authors note OTC costs would make the hurdle harder
replication_decay: Triggered the Bai-Bali-Wen retraction and is extended by the open 2026 factor-zoo replication
openness: DOI, repository manuscript, and companion corrected factors public
key_limitation: Pricing-model tests are not identical to implementable return-forecast tests

authors: Alexey Ivashchenko; Robert Kosowski
title: Transaction Costs and Capacity of Systematic Corporate Bond Strategies
target: Cost-adjusted strategy returns under modeled costs and zero-profit AUM capacity
predictor_family: Credit risk, drawdown, liquidity, reversal, and multifactor signals
model_family: Market-microstructure-invariance cost functions and capacity simulation
sample_design: Plain-vanilla bonds, October 2004-December 2022; main cost and capacity tests January 2010-December 2022
benchmark: Gross returns and conventional downward-sloping TRACE transaction-cost estimates
pit_status: PARTIAL — Signals are lagged; cost curves are estimated retrospectively and not validated with the strategy's own fills
native_result: Unrestricted reversal/liquidity capacity is about $0.9-$5.2 billion; low-turnover credit strategies reach hundreds of billions
costs_capacity: MMI costs rise with trade size; constraints lift reversal capacity to roughly $4.6-$10.3 billion
replication_decay: First detailed positive-slope capacity treatment in this lineage; no audited live execution by the cutoff
openness: DOI, SSRN, and open accepted manuscript; TRACE/FISD/CRSP inputs partly licensed
key_limitation: Modeled impact and mutual-fund return gaps are proxies, not realized strategy fills

authors: Alexander Dickerson; Cesare Robotti; Giulio Rossetti
title: The Corporate Bond Factor Replication Crisis
target: Monthly factor premia and bond-CAPM alpha
predictor_family: One hundred eight signals across nine credit-factor families
model_family: Error-corrected factor construction and portfolio sorts
sample_design: 52,656 bonds and 269 months, August 2002-December 2024; broad independent reconstruction
benchmark: Published factors and the corporate-bond market factor
pit_status: PIT — Explicitly removes correlated price-error bias and ex-post filtering look-ahead
native_result: Most factors lose significant alpha; six-month momentum falls from 0.30% monthly to zero after removing filtering bias
costs_capacity: Results are mainly gross; sparse trading, delay, and nonlinear impact imply additional erosion
replication_decay: Very recent preprint with no independent response by the cutoff, but open code and data facilitate audit
openness: Public preprint, corrected factors, Open Bond Asset Pricing resources, and PyBondLab software
key_limitation: Not yet peer reviewed; corrections depend on estimated latent efficient prices

authors: Jan Ericsson; Kris Jacobs; Rodolfo Oviedo
title: The Determinants of Credit Default Swap Premia
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
target: Five-year CDS spread levels and changes
horizon: Contemporaneous daily relation; not a forecast horizon
predictor_family: Leverage, equity volatility, and risk-free rates
model_family: Linear panel regressions and principal components
sample_design: CreditTrade quotes, 1999-2002; 4,813 bid and 5,436 offer observations after filters
benchmark: Minimal structural determinants and residual common-factor tests
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Quarterly balance-sheet values are linearly interpolated, making the design unsuitable as a PIT forecast
native_result: Leverage and volatility are statistically and economically important; residual common-factor evidence is limited
costs_capacity: Quoted CDS levels only; no executable bid-ask strategy, default settlement, or capital costs
replication_decay: Contrasts with corporate-bond spread nulls, but rests on an early, short, quote-based CDS sample
openness: Cambridge DOI and CIRANO PDF public; quote database proprietary
key_limitation: Contemporaneous fit with interpolated fundamentals is not affirmative forecast evidence

authors: Tyler Shumway
title: Forecasting Bankruptcy More Accurately: A Simple Hazard Model
target: Corporate bankruptcy
predictor_family: Accounting fundamentals, equity returns, size, and volatility
model_family: Discrete-time dynamic logit hazard
sample_design: NYSE/AMEX firms, 1962-1992; 300 bankruptcies and 39,745 firm-years with OOS comparisons
benchmark: Altman and Zmijewski static bankruptcy models
pit_status: PARTIAL — Market variables are lagged; historical accounting release delays are simplified
native_result: Combined hazard model places about 75% of bankrupt firms in the top risk decile and outperforms static alternatives
costs_capacity: Risk-ranking study; no lending, bond-trading, recovery, or intervention-cost mapping
replication_decay: Chava-Jarrow and later hazard studies independently support the dynamic-hazard advantage
openness: DOI, SSRN, and author PDF public; CRSP/Compustat inputs licensed
key_limitation: Small historical bankruptcy sample and incomplete point-in-time filing treatment

authors: Darrell Duffie; Leandro Saita; Ke Wang
title: Multi-Period Corporate Default Prediction with Stochastic Covariates
target: Conditional default probabilities
predictor_family: Distance-to-default, equity momentum, market returns, and rates
model_family: Doubly stochastic intensity model
sample_design: More than 390,000 firm-months, 1979-2004; fit through 1992 and test from 1993
benchmark: Moody's ratings, Watchlist/Outlook, and bond-yield-spread rankings
pit_status: PARTIAL — Forecasts use lagged market and rate covariates; exit labels and some firm data are finalized ex post
native_result: One-year OOS accuracy ratio is 88%; the worst 20% of firms contain about 92% of next-year defaults
costs_capacity: No recovery, exposure, capital, or trading decision loss
replication_decay: Later reduced-form default models broadly confirm ranking value; calibration varies by era and universe
openness: DOI, NBER, and author PDF public; core firm databases licensed
key_limitation: Conditional-independence assumption fails some clustering tests and crisis contagion is under-modeled

authors: Sreedhar T. Bharath; Tyler Shumway
title: Forecasting Default with the Merton Distance to Default Model
target: Next-quarter and one-year default
predictor_family: Structural distance-to-default, accounting, equity returns, and volatility
model_family: Merton structural score and hazard models
sample_design: CRSP/Compustat firms, 1980-2003; 1,449 defaults and 350,662 firm-quarter observations
benchmark: Naive Merton functional form and expanded reduced-form hazard
pit_status: PARTIAL — Quarterly sorts use lagged inputs; exact filing availability and proprietary KMV transformations are unavailable
native_result: Naive score puts 65.8% of defaults in the top decile versus 64.9% for Merton DD; expanded hazards do better
costs_capacity: No pricing, recovery, or portfolio-cost test
replication_decay: Later work commonly finds distance-to-default useful but not a sufficient default statistic
openness: DOI and author PDF public; CRSP, Compustat, and default histories licensed
key_limitation: Tests an academic approximation, not Moody's proprietary KMV implementation

authors: John Y. Campbell; Jens Hilscher; Jan Szilagyi
title: In Search of Distress Risk
target: Failure, bankruptcy, distress delisting, or D rating
horizon: H3-H5; one month to three years
predictor_family: Accounting, equity, size, past return, and volatility
model_family: Dynamic logit
sample_design: Monthly U.S. firm data, 1963-2003; annual rolling OOS coefficients from 1981
benchmark: Earlier distress scores, ratings, and simpler hazard specifications
pit_status: PARTIAL — Accounting variables are lagged; rolling fitting is chronological, while final failure labels are ex post
native_result: Rolling OOS fit is close to full-sample fit; persistent firm traits become more important at long horizons
costs_capacity: Default forecasting is not mapped to bond recovery, liquidity, or executable credit positions
replication_decay: The distress score is widely reused, though coefficients and calibration drift across eras
openness: DOI and NBER paper public; firm data licensed
key_limitation: Broad failure definition and late-sample concentration can flatter OOS stability

authors: Jun Pan; Kenneth J. Singleton
title: Default and Recovery Implicit in the Term Structure of Sovereign CDS Spreads
geography_market: Mexico, Turkey, and Korea sovereign CDS
target: CDS term structure, risk-neutral default arrival, and recovery
predictor_family: CDS curve, global event risk, volatility, and macro policy
model_family: Single-factor reduced-form intensity term structure
sample_design: Daily 1-, 2-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year quotes, March 2001-August 2006
benchmark: Observed cross-tenor CDS quotes and constant-loss specifications
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Contemporaneous curve fit; risk-premium correlations are full-sample and not OOS forecasts
native_result: One lognormal intensity factor captures most curve variation; inferred premia co-move with global risk measures
costs_capacity: Bid-ask is described, but no tradable timing or default-settlement strategy is tested
replication_decay: Longstaff and coauthors extend global-factor evidence to 26 sovereigns; crisis-era stability is untested here
openness: DOI and author PDFs public; dealer quotes proprietary
key_limitation: Only three sovereigns and model-dependent separation of default, recovery, and risk premia

authors: Francis A. Longstaff; Jun Pan; Lasse H. Pedersen; Kenneth J. Singleton
title: How Sovereign Is Sovereign Credit Risk?
geography_market: Twenty-six developed and emerging sovereign CDS markets
target: Monthly sovereign credit excess returns and spread components
predictor_family: Cross-asset global equity, volatility, bond, and credit premia
model_family: Principal components, spread decomposition, and predictive regressions
sample_design: Monthly sovereign CDS, October 2000-January 2010; cross-country portfolios
benchmark: Local macro variables and country-specific credit risk
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Predictors are ex ante market measures, but coefficients and portfolio choices use the full sample
native_result: First PC explains 64% of spreads; global premia explain about 15% of all-country and over 27% of Latin return variation
costs_capacity: Gross synthetic CDS returns; bid-ask, margin, counterparty, and crisis execution are incomplete
replication_decay: Global sovereign-risk comovement is widely supported; post-2010 and live timing evidence is absent
openness: AEA, NBER, and author versions public; CDS data proprietary
key_limitation: Short crisis-heavy sample and in-sample portfolio return regressions

authors: John M. Griffin; Dragon Yongjun Tang
title: Did Subjectivity Play a Role in CDO Credit Ratings?
geography_market: Global CDO issuance evaluated by a major rating agency
target: Subsequent CDO downgrades and tranche credit support
predictor_family: Rating-model overrides and collateral structure
model_family: Ordered logit, probit, and hazard models
sample_design: 916 CDOs issued January 1997-December 2007; $612.8 billion face value
benchmark: Rating agency's quantitative model and published default standards
pit_status: PIT — Issue-time model outputs and adjustments precede later downgrades
native_result: Larger positive overrides predict worse downgrades; 91.2% of pre-April-2007 AAA notes met only the agency's AA standard
costs_capacity: Estimates valuation consequences, not executable trading costs or tranche liquidity
replication_decay: Related surveillance-versus-ratings evidence supports bias; the exact agency and pre-crisis deal era limit transportability
openness: DOI, SSRN, and author PDF public; hand-collected agency data are not fully open
key_limitation: One agency and a selected issuance cohort during the structured-credit boom

authors: Victor DeMiguel; Lorenzo Garlappi; Raman Uppal
title: Optimal Versus Naive Diversification: How Inefficient Is the 1/N Portfolio Strategy?
geography_market: United States and international empirical portfolio datasets
target: Out-of-sample portfolio Sharpe ratio, certainty-equivalent return, and turnover
horizon: Monthly returns with rolling estimation and rebalancing (H4 decision problem)
predictor_family: Historical sample means and covariance matrices
model_family: Mean-variance optimization, Bayesian and shrinkage rules, minimum variance, and equal weighting
sample_design: Fourteen optimized allocation rules evaluated out of sample on seven empirical datasets with rolling estimation windows
benchmark: Naive 1/N equal-weight portfolio
pit_status: PIT — Rolling histories preserve forecast order; the study is based on return data rather than revised macro vintages
native_result: None of the optimized models consistently beat 1/N on Sharpe ratio, certainty-equivalent return, or turnover; estimation error overwhelmed theoretical gains at realistic sample lengths
costs_capacity: Turnover is an explicit evaluation dimension, but market impact, borrowing, financing, and scalable capacity are not fully modeled
replication_decay: Failure spans seven datasets inside the study; it is a broad benchmark result rather than an independently operated live replication
openness: Published article and author manuscript are public; underlying datasets are a mix of standard public and licensed sources
key_limitation: The menu and datasets represent classical allocation problems and do not cover newer nonlinear signals or institutional execution constraints

authors: Neil Gandal; JT Hamrick; Tyler Moore; Tali Oberman
title: Price Manipulation in the Bitcoin Ecosystem
geography_market: Mt. Gox and broader Bitcoin market
target: Daily Bitcoin returns and volume during suspicious trading
predictor_family: Events and suspicious exchange order flow
model_family: Event-day comparisons and robustness regressions
sample_design: Detailed leaked Mt. Gox transaction records over ten months in 2013, covering roughly 600,000 suspiciously acquired BTC.
benchmark: Days without suspicious trading activity
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable for forecasting: ex post forensic identification
native_result: Bitcoin prices rose on about 80% of suspicious-activity days versus about 55% otherwise, with roughly 4-5% average daily appreciation during suspicious activity.
costs_capacity: Not an implementable signal; demonstrates exchange counterparty and manipulation risk.
replication_decay: The exact Mt. Gox episode is unique, while later wash-trading research supports broader manipulation risk on unregulated venues.
openness: Public author manuscript and verified DOI; source records are unusual leaked exchange data rather than a recurring public feed.
key_limitation: One failed exchange and one historical episode; actor classification is ex post and does not generalize mechanically to current venues.

authors: Carlos Trucíos
title: Forecasting Bitcoin Risk Measures: A Robust Approach
target: One-day-ahead volatility and Value-at-Risk
predictor_family: Lagged returns and robust outlier treatment
model_family: Robust and conventional GARCH-family models; robust bootstrap VaR
sample_design: Daily Bitcoin returns from 2011-09-13 to 2017-12-31; rolling 1,000-day windows with five-minute realized measures for OOS evaluation.
benchmark: Non-robust GARCH-family volatility and VaR procedures
pit_status: PIT — for rolling lagged inputs; exchange and high-frequency source vintage is not fully archived
native_result: Robust procedures outperform non-robust alternatives for volatility loss and VaR backtests, showing that outliers materially affect Bitcoin risk forecasts.
costs_capacity: Risk-forecast study; no trading strategy or capacity claim.
replication_decay: Subsequent cryptocurrency VaR studies broadly retain the value of heavy tails, regimes, and combinations, but no prospective audit exists.
openness: Public manuscript via GARP and verified DOI; exact tick data and complete reproduction package are not archived.
key_limitation: Single asset and pre-2018 era; forecast usefulness is statistical and not mapped to a prespecified capital or trading decision.

authors: Carol Alexander; Michael Dakos
title: A Critical Investigation of Cryptocurrency Data and Analysis
geography_market: Global data vendors, ranking sites, and major exchanges
target: Validity of returns, betas, volatility models, and published crypto evidence
horizon: H2-H4: daily data and multi-year studies
predictor_family: Data-quality and timestamp audit
model_family: Cross-source reconciliation, literature audit, and Bayesian volatility calibration
sample_design: Cross-source BTC and ETH comparisons over 2016-2019 plus an audit of 152 published and discussion papers.
benchmark: Synchronized exchange-traded prices and correctly adjusted fiat or stablecoin cross-rates
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable: data-provenance audit
native_result: Only 25 of 152 audited papers use proper traded prices for the examined applications; ranking-site timestamp errors, nonconcurrent closes, Tether instability, and source choice materially alter betas and GARCH estimates.
costs_capacity: The audit shows that compromised volume and price data can invalidate liquidity, turnover, cost, and capacity estimates.
replication_decay: Later source-comparison studies confirm material divergence across cryptocurrency vendors and exchanges.
openness: Public SSRN manuscript and verified DOI; some compared commercial data are not redistributable.
key_limitation: The literature sample ends in 2019 and the audit does not re-estimate every affected paper's full conclusion.

authors: Igor Makarov; Antoinette Schoar
title: Trading and Arbitrage in Cryptocurrency Markets
target: Cross-exchange price deviations, arbitrage spreads, and return price formation
horizon: H1-H3: five minutes to several weeks
predictor_family: Microstructure, order flow, and venue fragmentation
model_family: Price-deviation decomposition and signed-volume regressions
sample_design: Tick data for BTC, ETH, and XRP on 34 exchanges in 19 countries, focused on 2017-01-01 to 2018-02-28.
benchmark: Law of one price; within-country and within-exchange cryptocurrency spreads
pit_status: PIT — for contemporaneous tick and signed-volume data; transfer settlement and account-access constraints are measured retrospectively
native_result: Large recurrent price gaps persist for hours to weeks, are much larger across countries than within countries, and widen during Bitcoin appreciations; common signed volume explains about 80% of Bitcoin returns.
costs_capacity: Capital controls, fiat transfer frictions, settlement delay, and exchange access constrain arbitrage; realized all-in fills and failure risk are not observed.
replication_decay: Venue leaders and spread magnitudes change as exchanges and regulations evolve, but fragmentation and transfer frictions recur in later market evidence.
openness: Public accepted manuscript; underlying Kaiko tick data are proprietary.
key_limitation: Observed price gaps are not guaranteed executable arbitrage after transfer delay, counterparty risk, capital controls, and simultaneous-leg constraints.

authors: Helder Sebastião; Pedro Godinho
title: Forecasting and Trading Cryptocurrencies with Machine Learning under Changing Market Conditions
target: Next-day return direction and strategy returns
predictor_family: Market data and on-chain network activity
model_family: Linear models, random forests, support-vector machines, and ensembles
sample_design: Daily data from 2015-08-15 to 2019-03-03; 648-day rolling training, a 324-day validation period, and a final untouched test quarter beginning 2018-04-13.
benchmark: Naive last-return forecast, individual models, and buy-and-hold
pit_status: PIT — for lagged features and chronological splits; exchange-data revision provenance is incomplete
native_result: The selected five-model ensemble earns test-period annualized cost-adjusted returns under the paper's 0.5% round-trip assumption of 9.62% for Ethereum and 5.73% for Litecoin; Bitcoin evidence is weaker.
costs_capacity: Assumes 0.5% proportional round-trip cost and no short selling; realized impact, funding, outages, and capacity are not tested.
replication_decay: No independent locked replication; later ML volatility evidence is heterogeneous by asset, and leakage-aware return benchmarks remain sparse.
openness: Open-access article and full text; code and exact exchange/network data snapshot are not archived.
key_limitation: Model selection maximizes validation-period trading returns across many configurations, leaving multiplicity and one-test-period dependence.

authors: Yukun Liu; Aleh Tsyvinski; Xi Wu
title: Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency
target: Cross-sectional weekly cryptocurrency returns
predictor_family: Characteristics and factors; momentum
model_family: Portfolio sorts and factor models
sample_design: Weekly panel of CoinMarketCap coins above $1 million in market capitalization beginning in 2014, including active and defunct coins; 25 candidate characteristics and long-short sorts.
benchmark: Cryptocurrency market factor and competing characteristic-factor models
pit_status: PARTIAL — weekly lagged characteristics are used, but exchange aggregation and historical constituent reconstruction are not fully audited
native_result: Market, size, and momentum factors span the significant alphas of the successful characteristic strategies in the discovery sample.
costs_capacity: Trading-cost robustness is reported, but short availability, delisting execution, market impact, and strategy capacity remain unresolved.
replication_decay: Ammann et al. find survivorship correction cuts the size premium roughly in half and removes positive one-week momentum; later momentum evidence remains heterogeneous.
openness: Public NBER manuscript and published DOI; complete production data and code are not archived.
key_limitation: Factor construction uses aggregated exchange data vulnerable to stale prices, fake volume, delistings, and non-executable short legs.

authors: Manuel Ammann; Tom Burdorf; Luca J. Liebi; Sebastian Stöckl
title: Survivorship and Delisting Bias in Cryptocurrency Markets
target: Portfolio returns and cross-sectional anomaly premia after delistings
horizon: H3-H4: weekly returns and annualized performance
predictor_family: Characteristics and factors; survivorship and delisting audit
model_family: Bias audit, portfolio sorts, and cross-sectional regressions
sample_design: Weekly point-in-time panel of 3,904 cryptocurrencies from 2014-01-07 to 2021-12-28 with manually collected delisting reasons and delisting returns.
benchmark: Survivor-only portfolios versus survivorship- and delisting-bias-free portfolios
pit_status: PIT — historical membership and delisting returns are reconstructed
native_result: Annualized survivor bias is 0.93% value-weighted and 62.19% equal-weighted; corrected size remains but is about 50% overstated, while one-week momentum, market beta, and downside risk show no positive relation to returns.
costs_capacity: No full fee, spread, impact, borrow, or capacity model.
replication_decay: The 2026 survivor-momentum study independently finds no stable payoff and strong sample dependence.
openness: Public SSRN paper and institutional manuscript; hand-collected delisting dataset and code are not fully public.
key_limitation: Working-paper status and dependence on reconstructed delisting prices and reasons that can be difficult to execute in real time.

authors: Lin William Cong; Xi Li; Ke Tang; Yang Yang
title: Crypto Wash Trading
target: Fake reported volume and temporary price distortion
predictor_family: Microstructure and forensic data-quality signals
model_family: Benford-law, rounding, and power-law forensic tests
sample_design: 448,475,535 BTC, ETH, LTC, and XRP trades from 29 exchanges, 2019-07-09 to 2019-11-03; regulated exchanges serve as authentic-trading controls.
benchmark: Digit, size-rounding, and tail distributions on regulated exchanges
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable: forensic audit of reported trades
native_result: Estimated wash trading averages more than 70% of reported volume on unregulated exchanges, improves rankings, and temporarily distorts prices.
costs_capacity: Not a strategy test; the result directly invalidates volume-based liquidity and capacity estimates on affected venues.
replication_decay: Consistent with independent suspicious-trading and fake-volume evidence; exact estimates remain venue- and period-specific.
openness: Public NBER and accepted-manuscript versions; TokenInsight transaction data are proprietary.
key_limitation: Only 29 API-compatible exchanges over roughly four months; forensic classification is model-based and cannot identify beneficial ownership.

authors: Alexander Brauneis; Mehmet Sahiner
title: Crypto Volatility Forecasting: Mounting a HAR, Sentiment, and Machine Learning Horserace
geography_market: Coinbase USD markets; eight major cryptocurrencies
target: Six-hour realized volatility
predictor_family: Lagged realized volatility and crypto-news sentiment
model_family: HAR, MLP, LSTM, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CNN-BiLSTM
sample_design: Five-minute Coinbase data aggregated to 1,461 six-hour observations for eight coins, 2021-12-21 to 2022-12-22; 1,169-observation rolling training window and 292 OOS forecasts.
benchmark: HAR realized-volatility model without sentiment
pit_status: PARTIAL — chronological rolling forecasts are used, but news-ingestion and AI-sentiment vintages are not fully versioned
native_result: ML models beat HAR for most coins but not Bitcoin; sentiment improves no-sentiment ML forecasts in 54.17% of cases and does not improve the linear HAR consistently.
costs_capacity: Decision value, trading costs, option liquidity, and capacity are not tested.
replication_decay: No independent post-publication replication; results cover one turbulent year and remain asset- and model-specific.
openness: Open-access article and public version of record; full proprietary news history and code are not archived.
key_limitation: Only 292 OOS observations per coin, overlapping model selection, one venue, and no economic-loss or execution evaluation.

authors: Yeguang Chi; Qionghua (Ruihua) Chu; Wenyan Hao
title: Return and Volatility Forecasting Using On-Chain Flows in Cryptocurrency Markets
geography_market: Global exchange flows for BTC, ETH, and USDT
target: Intraday BTC and ETH returns and volatility
predictor_family: On-chain and tokenomics variables; flows
model_family: Predictive regressions with in-sample and out-of-sample checks
sample_design: Wallet-to-exchange net inflows from 30 exchanges, 2017-12-16 to 2023-01-20; single- and double-variable models over five intraday horizons.
benchmark: Lagged-return or lagged-volatility controls and zero-predictability tests
pit_status: PARTIAL — lagged flows are used, but entity labeling and vendor revision timing are not version-audited
native_result: ETH inflows negatively predict ETH returns and volatility across horizons; USDT inflows predict selected BTC and ETH outcomes; BTC inflows generally do not predict BTC returns except at four hours.
costs_capacity: Illustrative ETH option scenarios are reported; realized spreads, fees, impact, labeling latency, and capacity are not fully modeled.
replication_decay: No independent exact replication or prospective archive identified by the cutoff.
openness: Public versioned arXiv paper; code and the complete vendor-derived entity-flow panel are not public.
key_limitation: Preprint-only evidence with many asset-horizon tests, unstable USDT results, and unresolved real-time address-label availability.

authors: Klaus Grobys; Davide Sandretto; Janne Äijö
title: On Survivor Cryptocurrency Momentum
target: Weekly cryptocurrency momentum returns
predictor_family: Momentum, reversal, trend, seasonality, and technical rules
model_family: Currency-style momentum portfolios
sample_design: Nine free-floating coins that remained in the top 100 and an annually refreshed top-30 universe, January 2017-August 2024.
benchmark: Zero payoff and the broader top-30 plain cryptocurrency momentum portfolio
pit_status: NOT-PIT — for the survivor portfolio: survival is defined ex post; the rotating top-30 diagnostic is closer to point-in-time
native_result: Survivor-coin momentum earns no significant payoff; the top-30 strategy is profitable only after trimming and is highly sample-dependent.
costs_capacity: Illiquidity is central to the design, but a full fees, spread, impact, and short-borrow implementation is absent.
replication_decay: Consistent with Grobys and Sapkota (2019) and the Ammann et al. survivorship audit; contradicts broad claims of stable crypto momentum.
openness: Open-access CC BY article and public repository copy.
key_limitation: The ex-post survivor component is invalid as an investable signal; the rotating top-30 diagnostic is closer to point-in-time but remains sample-dependent and lacks full execution costs.

authors: John Moody; Lizhong Wu; Yuansong Liao; Matthew Saffell
title: Performance Functions and Reinforcement Learning for Trading Systems and Portfolios
target: Trading position maximizing risk-adjusted return
predictor_family: Lagged returns and current portfolio state
model_family: Recurrent reinforcement learning and direct differential Sharpe-ratio optimization
sample_design: Historical train and out-of-sample trading simulations on a currency series and S&P 500, with proportional transaction costs
benchmark: Linear trading rules, supervised forecasting approaches, and buy-and-hold
pit_status: PARTIAL — Sequential features are lagged, but the small set of historical series and tuning process are not a modern nested point-in-time audit
native_result: Direct reinforcement of trading objectives outperforms several forecast-then-trade alternatives in the reported currency and equity-index simulations
costs_capacity: Proportional transaction costs enter the objective; spread variation, market impact, financing, and capacity are not modeled
replication_decay: The paper established a widely reused method, but the original two-market evidence is small and not independently live
openness: Published paper describes the algorithm; code and exact historical data pipeline are not released as a complete package
key_limitation: Few markets, limited holdouts, and in-simulation optimization leave high selection and regime risk

authors: Werner F. M. De Bondt; Richard Thaler
title: Does the Stock Market Overreact?
target: Long-horizon winner and loser portfolio returns
predictor_family: Long-term return reversal
model_family: Extreme portfolio event-time sorts
sample_design: CRSP monthly histories form extreme prior winner and loser portfolios and track multi-year subsequent returns.
benchmark: Prior winners and market-adjusted expected returns
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns; delisting, microcap, and historical execution details are incomplete.
native_result: Prior losers subsequently outperform prior winners, with especially large January returns, consistent with long-horizon overreaction.
costs_capacity: Gross extreme portfolios; historical spreads, delisting execution, shorting, and capacity are not fully modeled.
replication_decay: Long-run reversal is influential but sensitive to size, seasonality, microcaps, and overlapping-horizon inference.
openness: Verified DOI; CRSP construction is documented but the underlying database is licensed.
key_limitation: Small extreme portfolios and long overlapping horizons create dependence and specification sensitivity.

authors: Narasimhan Jegadeesh
title: Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns
target: Cross-sectional monthly abnormal returns
predictor_family: Short reversal and annual-lag return seasonality
model_family: Serial-correlation forecasts and decile portfolios
sample_design: Monthly 1934-1987 returns estimate lag-specific autocorrelation and form ten one-step-ahead forecast portfolios.
benchmark: No serial dependence and zero abnormal decile spread
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns; historical delisting and executable-price controls are incomplete.
native_result: Monthly first-order autocorrelation is negative, twelve-month correlation is strongly positive, and the extreme forecast-decile abnormal-return spread is 2.49% per month.
costs_capacity: No realistic turnover, spread, impact, shorting, or capacity deduction.
replication_decay: Subsequent work separates short reversal, medium momentum, and same-month seasonality and documents strong cost sensitivity.
openness: Verified DOI; reproducible CRSP design with licensed raw data.
key_limitation: A large gross spread from high-turnover extreme stocks is not an executable cost-adjusted strategy.

authors: William Brock; Josef Lakonishok; Blake LeBaron
title: Simple Technical Trading Rules and the Stochastic Properties of Stock Returns
geography_market: Dow Jones Industrial Average, United States
target: Index returns conditional on buy and sell signals
horizon: H2-H3: daily signals to multiweek positions
predictor_family: Moving-average and trading-range-break technical rules
model_family: Rule-based signals with bootstrap null models
sample_design: Twenty-six simple rules are tested on daily DJIA data from 1897-1986 against random-walk and fitted time-series bootstraps.
benchmark: Random walk, AR(1), GARCH-M, and exponential GARCH nulls
pit_status: PIT — for lagged index prices; historical constituent, dividend, and executable-price details are incomplete.
native_result: Buy signals have higher and less volatile returns than sell signals, and observed rule returns reject all four fitted null models.
costs_capacity: No full transaction-cost, slippage, shorting, dividend, or capacity treatment.
replication_decay: A later Reality Check finds historical significance but no superior performance in the 1987-1996 holdout or S&P 500 futures.
openness: Verified DOI; rules and bootstrap design are disclosed, with public index history.
key_limitation: The rule set and long historical sample were analyzed retrospectively without realistic execution.

authors: Eugene F. Fama; Kenneth R. French
title: The Cross-Section of Expected Stock Returns
geography_market: NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ, United States
target: Cross-sectional monthly stock returns
predictor_family: Size, book-to-market, leverage, earnings-price, and beta
model_family: Fama-MacBeth cross-sectional regressions and portfolio sorts
sample_design: U.S. common stocks, 1963-1990; contemporaneously specified characteristic sorts and monthly cross-sectional regressions.
benchmark: CAPM market beta
pit_status: PARTIAL — accounting data are lagged, but modern point-in-time vendor controls were unavailable.
native_result: Size and book-to-market capture average-return variation associated with beta and other characteristics; the beta-return relation is flat after controls.
costs_capacity: Gross value-weighted portfolio evidence; no comprehensive turnover, spread, borrow, or impact analysis.
replication_decay: Extensively replicated, but later work documents specification, microcap, era, and publication-decay heterogeneity.
openness: Verified DOI; factor and portfolio updates are publicly maintained, while security-level source data are licensed.
key_limitation: Exploratory in-sample sorting cannot distinguish risk compensation from mispricing or guarantee implementable forecasts.

authors: Narasimhan Jegadeesh; Sheridan Titman
title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency
target: Winner-minus-loser portfolio return
predictor_family: Cross-sectional price momentum
model_family: Formation-holding portfolio sorts
sample_design: U.S. stocks are ranked on past three- to twelve-month returns and held for three to twelve months over 1965-1989.
benchmark: Zero abnormal return after systematic-risk adjustment
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns; historical bid-ask, delisting, and short-borrow records are incomplete.
native_result: Buying past winners and selling losers produces significant positive three- to twelve-month returns not explained by measured systematic risk; profits later dissipate.
costs_capacity: Original results are gross and omit a complete spread, impact, borrow, financing, and capacity model.
replication_decay: Replicated internationally and over later eras, but magnitudes decay and cost-adjusted profitability depends strongly on liquidity and construction.
openness: Verified DOI; transparent CRSP portfolio design with licensed source data.
key_limitation: Discovery-sample portfolio sorts and gross returns do not establish scalable alpha.

authors: K. Geert Rouwenhorst
title: International Momentum Strategies
target: International winner-minus-loser return
predictor_family: Cross-sectional price momentum
model_family: Country-neutral international portfolio sorts
sample_design: Past-return portfolios across twelve countries from 1980-1995 test the U.S. momentum pattern externally.
benchmark: Country-adjusted loser portfolios and risk-adjusted zero return
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns; historical international survivorship and execution controls are incomplete.
native_result: Past winners outperform losers by more than 1% per month after risk correction; continuation appears in all twelve countries and lasts about one year.
costs_capacity: Gross returns; international spreads, taxes, borrow, currency conversion, and capacity are not deducted.
replication_decay: Strong independent geographic replication of U.S. momentum; later cost and crowding studies qualify implementability.
openness: Verified DOI and disclosed construction; underlying international security data are proprietary.
key_limitation: A short developed-market era and gross long-short returns overstate executable breadth.

authors: Eugene F. Fama; Kenneth R. French
title: Value versus Growth: The International Evidence
target: Value-minus-growth portfolio returns
predictor_family: Book-to-market value characteristic
model_family: International portfolio sorts and factor regressions
sample_design: Country and global value-growth portfolios cover thirteen markets from 1975-1995.
benchmark: International CAPM and growth portfolios
pit_status: PARTIAL — accounting variables are lagged; historical international database biases remain possible.
native_result: Global high-minus-low book-to-market portfolios earn 7.68% per year, and value beats growth in twelve of thirteen markets.
costs_capacity: Gross portfolio returns; country-specific spreads, taxes, shorting, and capacity are not deducted.
replication_decay: Value is widely replicated across markets and asset classes but experiences long drawdowns, crowding, and regime variation.
openness: Verified DOI and public portfolio methodology; underlying international security data are proprietary.
key_limitation: A 21-year selected developed-market sample is not a prospective implementation test.

authors: Robert A. Korajczyk; Ronnie Sadka
title: Are Momentum Profits Robust to Trading Costs?
target: Cost-adjusted momentum return under modeled costs and break-even capacity
predictor_family: Cross-sectional momentum
model_family: Intraday price-impact model and liquidity-weighted portfolios
sample_design: Intraday data estimate proportional and nonlinear impact; equal-, value-, liquidity-, and hybrid-weighted momentum strategies are compared.
benchmark: Zero abnormal return after estimated trading costs
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns and contemporaneous intraday cost estimation; fills remain simulated.
native_result: Liquidity and hybrid weighting preserve momentum profitability with estimated break-even fund size of at least $5 billion in December 1999 dollars.
costs_capacity: Explicit spread, nonlinear impact, portfolio-size, and break-even-capacity analysis; borrow and operations remain incomplete.
replication_decay: Counters the strongest cost-null result and establishes that optimized implementation matters; later eras still show decay and crowding risk.
openness: Verified DOI with detailed cost equations; TAQ and CRSP inputs are licensed.
key_limitation: Estimated impact and one historical liquidity regime are not realized live execution.

authors: David A. Lesmond; Michael J. Schill; Chunsheng Zhou
title: The illusory nature of momentum profits
target: Cost-adjusted relative-strength strategy return under modeled costs
predictor_family: Cross-sectional momentum
model_family: Momentum portfolios with security-level trading-cost estimates
sample_design: Standard winner-loser strategies are mapped to proportional trading-cost proxies, emphasizing the costly securities generating gross momentum.
benchmark: Gross momentum return minus estimated round-trip trading costs
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns; historical cost estimates are modeled rather than realized fills.
native_result: High gross momentum profits occur in high-cost stocks; estimated frequent-trading costs prevent profitable execution and leave little evidence against no arbitrage.
costs_capacity: Explicit security-level proportional-cost treatment; market impact, borrow, and institutional execution remain approximate.
replication_decay: Later intraday cost work finds more favorable liquidity-weighted implementations, so the cost-adjusted verdict is construction-dependent.
openness: Verified DOI and public full-text copy; licensed return data and estimated cost inputs are required.
key_limitation: Cost proxies may overstate institutional execution costs and do not model optimized trading.

authors: Yuriy Nevmyvaka; Yi Feng; Michael Kearns
title: Reinforcement Learning for Optimized Trade Execution
venue: Proceedings of the 23rd International Conference on Machine Learning: 673-680
target: Execution shortfall for large parent orders
predictor_family: Limit-order-book state, elapsed time, remaining inventory, and execution history
model_family: Q-learning with carefully structured state and action spaces
sample_design: Four years of high-frequency limit-order data with extensive historical execution simulation and out-of-sample policy comparisons
benchmark: Fixed-schedule and domain-informed execution strategies
pit_status: PIT — Order-book events are historical and sequenced, but the simulator cannot reproduce every queue, latency, hidden-liquidity, and self-impact effect
native_result: The learned policy reduces execution cost relative to benchmark strategies, and strong domain-knowledge constraints materially improve learning and performance
costs_capacity: Execution cost is the native objective; counterfactual market impact, queue position, fees, and capacity under the agent's own orders remain approximated
replication_decay: A large proprietary dataset supports robustness inside one market setting; independent public replication is blocked by data access
openness: Conference paper is public; the proprietary order-book data, simulator, and production system are not
key_limitation: Historical replay assumes the market would not change in response to the learned order flow

authors: Ivo Welch; Amit Goyal
title: A Comprehensive Look at The Empirical Performance of Equity Premium Prediction
target: Equity premium
predictor_family: Valuation and macroeconomic variables
model_family: Univariate predictive regressions
sample_design: Annual 1872-2005 and monthly 1927-2005 U.S. data; recursive pseudo-out-of-sample comparison of published predictors.
benchmark: Expanding historical-mean equity-premium forecast
pit_status: PARTIAL — predictors are lagged, but real-time vintages are not reconstructed uniformly.
native_result: Most published variables forecast poorly in and out of sample; models are unstable and do not profitably time the market relative to the historical mean.
costs_capacity: No full spread, impact, financing, or capacity model; utility results are frictionless.
replication_decay: Foundational adverse benchmark; later constrained and combination methods recover gains only for narrower specifications on overlapping data.
openness: Public DOI metadata and author-maintained predictor data; underlying market series are largely public.
key_limitation: The recursively evaluated period became the field's repeatedly consulted test set.

authors: John Y. Campbell; Samuel B. Thompson
title: Predicting Excess Stock Returns Out of Sample: Can Anything Beat the Historical Average?
target: Excess market return
predictor_family: Valuation and macroeconomic variables
model_family: Sign-constrained predictive regressions
sample_design: Recursive U.S. forecasts using the Goyal-Welch predictor set, with coefficient-sign and forecast-sign restrictions imposed at each origin.
benchmark: Historical-average excess return
pit_status: PARTIAL — lag discipline is explicit; macro and accounting vintages are not fully archived.
native_result: Many restricted regressions beat the historical average; out-of-sample explanatory power is small but economically meaningful for mean-variance investors.
costs_capacity: Portfolio utility is reported without realistic turnover, impact, financing, or taxes.
