replication_decay: Frequently reproduced on the same public predictor panel; gains remain sensitive to restriction, evaluation window, and utility assumptions.
openness: Public DOI and reproducible public-series design; no complete versioned code package.
key_limitation: Restrictions were motivated after broad knowledge of failures on the shared test period.

authors: Steven L. Heston; Ronnie Sadka
title: Seasonality in the cross-section of stock returns
target: Same-calendar-month cross-sectional returns
horizon: H4-H6: annual lags up to twenty years
predictor_family: Return seasonality
model_family: Lag-specific portfolio sorts and autocorrelation decomposition
sample_design: CRSP stocks are ranked by returns in the same calendar month at annual lags, controlling for momentum, reversal, size, industry, events, and fiscal year.
benchmark: Nonseasonal past-return strategies and standard characteristic controls
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns; historical delisting and execution controls are incomplete.
native_result: Same-month return persistence lasts up to twenty annual lags, with reported seasonal decile spreads above 50 basis points per month.
costs_capacity: Gross monthly rebalancing returns; spreads, short borrow, impact, and capacity are not comprehensively deducted.
replication_decay: Later international and multi-asset studies replicate seasonality, while emerging-market strength is heterogeneous.
openness: Verified DOI and public author manuscript; CRSP security data are licensed.
key_limitation: Many lag choices and a retrospectively discovered periodic structure create search risk.

authors: David E. Rapach; Jack K. Strauss; Guofu Zhou
title: Out-of-Sample Equity Premium Prediction: Combination Forecasts and Links to the Real Economy
target: Equity premium
predictor_family: Valuation and macroeconomic variables
model_family: Forecast combinations
sample_design: Expanding-window monthly forecasts combine many univariate predictive regressions and evaluate stability across recursive subperiods.
benchmark: Historical-average forecast and individual predictive regressions
pit_status: PARTIAL — regressors are lagged; full real-time macro vintages are not used.
native_result: Combination forecasts deliver statistically and economically significant gains over the historical average more consistently than unstable individual models.
costs_capacity: Mean-variance utility is frictionless; implementation turnover and impact are not comprehensively modeled.
replication_decay: A durable methodological result across later studies, although many tests reuse the same U.S. predictor database and eras.
openness: Public DOI and standard public predictor panel; published article and appendices identify construction.
key_limitation: Retrospective combination choices and a repeatedly reused evaluation sample weaken holdout status.

authors: Miguel A. Ferreira; Pedro Santa-Clara
title: Forecasting stock market returns: The sum of the parts is more than the whole
target: Total market return
predictor_family: Cash flows, valuation, and payout components
model_family: Present-value component forecast
sample_design: Expanding-window forecasts separately model dividend-price, earnings-growth, and price-earnings-growth components, then sum them.
benchmark: Historical mean and conventional predictive regressions
pit_status: PARTIAL — return components are lagged; accounting restatements and vintage availability are not fully reconstructed.
native_result: Out-of-sample R-squared exceeds 1.3% monthly and 13.4% annually; the reported market-timing Sharpe-ratio gain is 0.3.
costs_capacity: Reported timing performance is gross and omits trading impact, financing, and taxes.
replication_decay: Later sum-of-parts variants report gains, but independent frozen prospective validation is absent.
openness: Verified journal DOI plus public NBER version; inputs and equations are disclosed.
key_limitation: Large annual gains rely on few nonoverlapping observations and a retrospectively studied U.S. history.

authors: Thomas Dangl; Michael Halling
title: Predictive regressions with time-varying coefficients
target: Monthly excess index return
predictor_family: Valuation, cross-sectional premium, and macro variables
model_family: Bayesian model averaging with drifting coefficients
sample_design: Monthly May 1937-December 2002 data; strict recursive forecasts compare time-varying and constant-coefficient systems.
benchmark: Historical mean and constant-coefficient predictive regressions
pit_status: PARTIAL — each forecast uses prior observations only; source-series vintages are not fully archived.
native_result: Time-varying models beat both benchmarks and yield reported annual utility gains of 1.8%-5.8%, with stronger predictability in recessions.
costs_capacity: Utility calculations do not include a complete trading-cost, financing, or impact model.
replication_decay: No locked prospective archive; later regime-aware studies are supportive but use overlapping U.S. data.
openness: Verified DOI and accessible article text; model and forecast timing are documented.
key_limitation: Flexible drift and model averaging were evaluated retrospectively on a finite set of business cycles.

authors: Bryan T. Kelly; Seth Pruitt
title: Market Expectations in the Cross-Section of Present Values
geography_market: United States market and characteristic portfolios
target: Aggregate and portfolio returns
predictor_family: Cross-sectional valuation ratios
model_family: Partial least squares latent-factor system
sample_design: A latent factor extracted from the cross-section of book-to-market ratios is estimated recursively and used for market and portfolio forecasts.
benchmark: Historical mean and conventional aggregate predictors
pit_status: PARTIAL — accounting variables are lagged, but the historical database is not fully point-in-time versioned.
native_result: The latent valuation factor produces out-of-sample return R-squared of 13% annually and 0.9% monthly, with similar evidence for value, size, momentum, and industry portfolios.
costs_capacity: Forecast accuracy is primary; portfolio costs, impact, shorting, and capacity are not fully evaluated.
replication_decay: Related latent-factor and IPCA work supports the mechanism, largely within connected author and data lineages.
openness: Verified DOI and public working-paper versions; construction is documented but core CRSP/Compustat data are licensed.
key_limitation: Cross-sectional information and target returns come from the same U.S. equity system, limiting independent validation.

authors: Clifford S. Asness; Tobias J. Moskowitz; Lasse Heje Pedersen
title: Value and Momentum Everywhere
geography_market: Global individual equities and equity indexes
target: Value and momentum long-short returns
predictor_family: Value and momentum
model_family: Cross-market factor portfolios and three-factor model
sample_design: Common value and momentum definitions are applied across diverse countries and asset classes; this record scopes the equity evidence.
benchmark: Local and global passive market factors
pit_status: PARTIAL — price signals are point-in-time and fundamentals lagged; historical global data vintages vary.
native_result: Value and momentum premia are consistent across eight markets and asset classes; they share global structure and are negatively correlated with each other.
costs_capacity: Gross factors; the paper discusses liquidity risk but does not deduct complete realized costs and impact for every market.
replication_decay: Substantial cross-market replication; later crowding, crash, cost, and post-publication evidence shows time variation rather than disappearance.
openness: Verified DOI and transparent common construction; much underlying global data are proprietary.
key_limitation: Pooling related markets does not create independent prospective observations, and cost-adjusted scalability is unverified.

authors: Christopher J. Neely; David E. Rapach; Jun Tu; Guofu Zhou
title: Forecasting the Equity Risk Premium: The Role of Technical Indicators
target: Equity risk premium
predictor_family: Technical rules plus macroeconomic variables
model_family: Predictive regressions and forecast combinations
sample_design: Recursive monthly forecasts compare moving-average and momentum indicators, macro predictors, and combined information.
benchmark: Historical mean; macro-only and technical-only forecasts
pit_status: PARTIAL — price indicators are point-in-time; some macro series are not real-time vintages.
native_result: Technical indicators show statistically and economically significant in- and out-of-sample power; combining them with macro variables improves forecasts further.
costs_capacity: Asset-allocation gains are not a full realized-cost or capacity test.
replication_decay: Supplemental data aid reproduction; no independent prospective forecast record is established.
openness: Publisher supplemental data are linked at the verified DOI.
key_limitation: Many correlated rules and repeated use of the standard U.S. return-prediction sample raise selection risk.

authors: Eugene F. Fama; Kenneth R. French
title: A five-factor asset pricing model
target: Average returns on characteristic portfolios
predictor_family: Size, value, profitability, and investment characteristics
model_family: Linear factor model
sample_design: July 1963-December 2013 U.S. portfolios sorted on size, book-to-market, operating profitability, and investment.
benchmark: Fama-French three-factor model
pit_status: PARTIAL — portfolio inputs are conventionally lagged; database revisions are not fully vintage-controlled.
native_result: The model explains 71%-94% of expected-return variation in targeted portfolios and beats the three-factor model, but is rejected and misses small, low-profitability aggressive-investment stocks.
costs_capacity: Factor returns are gross; no strategy-level spread, impact, borrow, or capacity validation.
replication_decay: International tests broadly support several patterns but expose regional failures; momentum remains outside the model.
openness: Verified DOI and public factor returns; underlying CRSP/Compustat data are licensed.
key_limitation: Factors and test portfolios are selected and evaluated in the same sample.

authors: Kewei Hou; Chen Xue; Lu Zhang
title: Digesting Anomalies: An Investment Approach
target: Cross-sectional average returns and anomaly alphas
predictor_family: Investment and profitability characteristics
model_family: q-factor linear factor model
sample_design: A common U.S. construction examines nearly 80 published anomalies against market, size, investment, and profitability factors.
benchmark: Fama-French three-factor and Carhart four-factor models
pit_status: PARTIAL — accounting lags are imposed; historical data vintages are not fully frozen.
native_result: About half of examined anomalies are insignificant in broad tests; the q-factor model matches or improves on standard models for most remaining significant anomalies.
costs_capacity: Gross factor and anomaly returns; no complete implementation-cost or capacity assessment.
replication_decay: The model became a major benchmark; later large replications support many failures but dispute exact replication rates and constructions.
openness: Verified DOI and public author factor library; security-level source data remain licensed.
key_limitation: Factor discovery and anomaly digestion are largely in-sample and sensitive to portfolio conventions.

authors: Campbell R. Harvey; Yan Liu; Heqing Zhu
title: … and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
target: Statistical credibility of factor return claims
predictor_family: Characteristics and factors
model_family: Dependence-aware multiple-testing framework
sample_design: Historical factor discoveries since 1967 are mapped into time-varying significance hurdles under multiple testing.
benchmark: Conventional absolute t-statistic threshold of 1.96
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable to signal timestamps; publication chronology defines the information set.
native_result: A newly proposed factor generally needs a t-statistic above 3.0; the authors argue most claimed findings are likely false under the expanded search universe.
costs_capacity: No trading implementation test; the contribution is statistical screening.
replication_decay: Later replications confirm multiplicity is material but disagree sharply on the fraction of true factors.
openness: Verified DOI with documented factor census and methods; no single raw-data package covers the literature.
key_limitation: The unobserved number and dependence of researcher trials must be estimated rather than observed.

authors: Robert Novy-Marx; Mihail Velikov
title: A Taxonomy of Anomalies and Their Trading Costs
target: Cost-adjusted characteristic-anomaly returns under modeled costs
horizon: H3-H4: monthly rebalancing and longer holding
predictor_family: Characteristics and anomalies
model_family: Cost-mitigated buy-hold-spread portfolios
sample_design: Anomaly strategies are grouped by turnover and rebuilt with asymmetric entry and continuation bands to reduce trading.
benchmark: Gross anomaly spreads and naive monthly rebalancing
pit_status: PARTIAL — signals are conventionally lagged; costs are estimated rather than realized and vintage controls vary.
native_result: Most anomalies below 50% monthly turnover retain significant cost-adjusted spreads under the paper's assumptions; few higher-turnover anomalies do, and size/value have greatest capacity.
costs_capacity: Explicit turnover and transaction-cost mitigation plus relative capacity; borrow, financing, taxes, and full impact are incomplete.
replication_decay: Supports low-turnover anomalies while sharply attenuating high-turnover claims; later cost estimates refine but do not erase the ranking.
openness: Verified DOI with Internet Appendix and reproducible portfolio rules; raw data are licensed.
key_limitation: Modeled costs and optimized bands are not audited fills, and tuning uses historical data.

authors: R. David McLean; Jeffrey Pontiff
title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
target: Post-sample and post-publication anomaly returns
predictor_family: Ninety-seven published cross-sectional predictors
model_family: Event-time meta-regressions and portfolio sorts
sample_design: Returns for 97 predictors are partitioned into original, post-sample, and post-publication periods.
benchmark: Original in-sample predictor returns
pit_status: PIT — for publication dates and lagged portfolio signals; underlying accounting vintage controls vary by study.
native_result: Predictor returns are 26% lower out of sample and 58% lower after publication; the estimated publication-informed trading effect is 32 percentage points.
costs_capacity: No unified realized-cost model; decay is larger in high-idiosyncratic-risk, low-liquidity stocks.
replication_decay: Direct evidence of substantial decay, while positive average returns remain and international decay differs.
openness: Verified DOI; predictor list and construction details are disclosed, with licensed source data.
key_limitation: Publication timing is endogenous and post-publication decline mixes arbitrage, bias, and secular market change.

authors: Matti Keloharju; Juhani T. Linnainmaa; Peter Nyberg
title: Return Seasonalities
geography_market: United States stocks and international equity indexes
target: Seasonal strategy and anomaly returns
predictor_family: Same-calendar-period return seasonality
model_family: Seasonal portfolio sorts across signals and markets
sample_design: Same-month histories predict U.S. stock returns; extensions test anomalies, international equity indexes, commodities, and daily frequency.
benchmark: Unconditional expected returns and nonseasonal strategies
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns and calendar mapping; historical execution details vary across markets.
native_result: A same-calendar-month stock strategy earns 13% per year, with related seasonalities in anomalies and international indexes.
costs_capacity: Gross returns; turnover, spreads, borrow, impact, and strategy capacity are not fully modeled.
replication_decay: Broad cross-market extension supports the pattern, but mechanisms and implementation after costs remain unresolved.
openness: Verified DOI with documented tests; several underlying data sets require licenses.
key_limitation: Multiple related seasonal strategies are examined without a frozen prospective selection rule.

authors: Jeremiah Green; John R. M. Hand; X. Frank Zhang
title: The Characteristics that Provide Independent Information about Average U.S. Monthly Stock Returns
target: Cross-sectional monthly returns
predictor_family: Ninety-four firm characteristics
model_family: Simultaneous Fama-MacBeth regressions and hedge portfolios
sample_design: Ninety-four characteristics enter jointly over 1980-2014 with microcap controls and data-snooping adjustment; post-2003 evidence is isolated.
benchmark: Zero incremental coefficient and zero characteristic-hedge return
pit_status: PARTIAL — accounting variables are lagged; the characteristic menu is selected from prior literature.
native_result: Twelve characteristics are reliable over the full sample, only two remain independently reliable after 2003, and nonmicrocap hedge returns are insignificantly different from zero post-2003.
costs_capacity: Microcaps are de-emphasized, but spreads, borrow, impact, and capacity are not fully modeled.
replication_decay: Strong later-era attenuation aligns with publication-decay evidence and conflicts with broader positive replication counts.
openness: Verified DOI and detailed appendices; source CRSP/Compustat data are licensed.
key_limitation: Joint regression estimates are sensitive to collinearity and the chosen characteristic definitions.

authors: Thomas Fischer; Christopher Krauss
title: Deep Learning with Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Financial Market Predictions
target: Next-day stock return direction and cross-sectional portfolio return
predictor_family: Lagged daily stock returns
model_family: Long short-term memory network
sample_design: Rolling out-of-sample evaluation from 1992-2015 with chronological training and comparisons across subperiods
benchmark: Random forest, deep neural network, logistic regression, and buy-and-hold market exposure
pit_status: PARTIAL — Signals are chronological and based on historical membership data; close-to-close execution timing and full data-vintage replay are not audited
native_result: The LSTM earned strong gross and 5-basis-point-cost performance over the full sample, but the daily long-short edge decayed to approximately zero in the 2010-2015 subperiod
costs_capacity: A fixed 5-basis-point half-turn cost is applied; borrow, bid-ask variation, market impact, and capacity of frequent rebalancing are omitted
replication_decay: The paper's own late-sample split shows pronounced decay, weakening the headline full-history result
openness: Published manuscript and implementation details are public; exact market data require licensed sources
key_limitation: A high-turnover strategy and a weak final subperiod make the result highly sensitive to execution and regime choice

authors: Juhani T. Linnainmaa; Michael R. Roberts
title: The History of the Cross-Section of Stock Returns
geography_market: United States common stocks over the twentieth century
target: Accounting-anomaly portfolio returns
predictor_family: Accounting characteristics
model_family: Historical backcast and forward out-of-sample portfolio tests
sample_design: Hand-collected pre-Compustat data extend accounting anomalies backward, while later data test them forward beyond discovery samples.
benchmark: Original anomaly-sample returns and Sharpe ratios
pit_status: PARTIAL — historical statements are aligned conservatively, but exact vintage and survivorship controls vary.
native_result: Most accounting-based anomalies, including investment, weaken backward and forward in time; average returns and Sharpe ratios fall while correlations rise.
costs_capacity: Gross portfolios; historical trading costs and modern impact are not comprehensively reconstructed.
replication_decay: Fresh historical data provide independent adverse evidence; a few anomalies persist with economic interpretation.
openness: Verified DOI with Internet Appendix; hand-collected and licensed components limit turnkey reproduction.
key_limitation: Earlier accounting regimes and market structure differ materially from the discovery era.

authors: Bryan T. Kelly; Seth Pruitt; Yinan Su
title: Characteristics are covariances: A unified model of risk and return
target: One-month stock returns and cross-sectional pricing errors
predictor_family: Firm characteristics as instruments for time-varying loadings
model_family: Instrumented principal component analysis
sample_design: Stock-level characteristics estimate latent factors and dynamic loadings; recursive forecasts are compared with observed-factor and PCA models.
benchmark: Fama-French five-factor and conventional PCA factor models
pit_status: PARTIAL — characteristics are lagged; the licensed panel is not a fully archived vintage database.
native_result: Five IPCA factors deliver monthly out-of-sample predictive R-squared of 0.6%, more than doubling the five-factor model's in-sample fit; only ten characteristics are significant at 1%.
costs_capacity: Forecast and SDF portfolios are gross; turnover, impact, borrow, leverage, and capacity are incomplete.
replication_decay: Influential ML-factor benchmark with related same-lineage extensions; independent locked replication remains limited.
openness: Verified DOI and public NBER version; core CRSP/Compustat panel is licensed.
key_limitation: The flexible latent model is judged on a retrospectively reused U.S. panel without realized implementation.

authors: Zheng Tracy Ke; Bryan T. Kelly; Dacheng Xiu
title: Predicting Returns with Text Data
target: Firm-level returns after Dow Jones Newswires articles
predictor_family: Timestamped financial news text
model_family: Supervised predictive screening, topic weighting, and penalized-likelihood sentiment scoring
sample_design: 1989-2017 news and returns with rolling 15-year windows: ten years training, five validation, then sequential out-of-sample tests from 2004-2017
benchmark: Dictionary sentiment, commercial vendor sentiment, market model, and unsupervised text methods
pit_status: PIT — Articles are timestamped, models use only prior rolling windows, and trades are delayed to a feasible post-news price; vendor feed archival details remain proprietary
native_result: Supervised sentiment predicts post-news returns and limits-to-arbitrage patterns; the strategy reports a cost-adjusted Sharpe ratio up to about 2.30 under the paper's 10-basis-point daily cost assumption.
costs_capacity: Daily turnover is roughly 90%-94%; the study charges 10 basis points and imposes turnover aversion, but market impact, borrow, latency, and capacity remain simplified
replication_decay: Long rolling tests and explicit costs are strong retrospective evidence; the same licensed feed and research team supply the full result
openness: NBER paper and method are public; Dow Jones Newswires text and some return data are licensed
key_limitation: Very high turnover and proprietary text make independent executable replication difficult

authors: Justin Sirignano; Rama Cont
title: Universal Features of Price Formation in Financial Markets: Perspectives from Deep Learning
target: Next mid-price move from the limit order book
predictor_family: Full-depth limit-order-book state and order-flow history
model_family: Pooled deep neural network with recurrent components
sample_design: Billions of order-book events for 489 stocks, with chronological test months and a separate set of stocks excluded from training
benchmark: Stock-specific models and linear order-book predictors
pit_status: PIT — Exchange events are strictly timestamped; deployable latency, queue position, and feed handling are not reproduced
native_result: A model trained across many stocks predicts price-move direction better than asset-specific alternatives and generalizes to stocks absent from training
costs_capacity: The paper evaluates classification, not executable alpha; spread crossing, queue priority, latency, fees, impact, and capacity are outside scope
replication_decay: Cross-stock transfer is an internal externalization test, not an independent-team replication or live strategy
openness: Paper and architecture are public; the full proprietary high-frequency order-book dataset and production code are not
key_limitation: Statistical price-direction accuracy at event horizons does not establish executable profitability after costs.

authors: Heiko Jacobs; Sebastian Müller
title: Anomalies across the globe: Once public, no longer existent?
geography_market: Thirty-nine developed and international stock markets
target: Pre- and post-publication anomaly returns
predictor_family: Two hundred forty-one cross-sectional anomalies
model_family: Country-level portfolio meta-analysis
sample_design: More than two million anomaly country-months compare pre-sample, post-sample, and post-publication behavior in 39 markets.
benchmark: Pre-publication long-short anomaly returns
pit_status: PIT — for publication chronology and lagged signals; underlying accounting-vintage quality differs by country.
native_result: The United States is the only country with a reliable post-publication decline; international anomaly returns remain strong post-sample and post-publication.
costs_capacity: Arbitrage-cost proxies explain cross-country variation, but realized trade costs and capacity are not fully deducted.
replication_decay: Externally qualifies the U.S. decay result: decay is strong domestically but not universal internationally.
openness: Verified DOI plus public working-paper text; commercial international equity data constrain full reproduction.
key_limitation: Cross-country histories, coverage, liquidity, and anomaly discovery origins are unequal.

authors: Shihao Gu; Bryan Kelly; Dacheng Xiu
title: Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning
target: One-month stock excess returns and portfolio performance
predictor_family: Firm characteristics and macro interactions
model_family: Trees, neural networks, regularized linear models, and ensembles
sample_design: U.S. stocks from 1957-2016 use rolling training, validation, and a chronological 1987-2016 test; model classes share the same predictors.
benchmark: Leading linear and regression-based characteristic strategies
pit_status: PARTIAL — predictors are lagged within the pipeline, but the curated characteristic set was known ex post and vendor vintages are incomplete.
native_result: Trees and neural networks perform best, with some ML portfolios roughly doubling leading regression-strategy performance; momentum, liquidity, and volatility dominate.
costs_capacity: Reported portfolios are mainly gross; turnover, impact, borrow, leverage, and capacity are not jointly stress-tested.
replication_decay: Widely reproduced as a benchmark; later real-time feature-universe and cost studies find materially smaller gains.
openness: Public code and working-paper materials exist; CRSP/Compustat inputs require licenses.
key_limitation: The long test period informed subsequent model development and curated features embed publication knowledge.

authors: Kewei Hou; Chen Xue; Lu Zhang
title: Replicating Anomalies
target: Raw and risk-adjusted anomaly returns
predictor_family: Four hundred fifty-two published anomalies
model_family: Standardized portfolio sorts and cross-sectional regressions
sample_design: A common library applies NYSE breakpoints, value weighting, microcap mitigation, and single- plus multiple-testing hurdles to 452 anomalies.
benchmark: Original claims; absolute t-statistic thresholds of 1.96 and 2.78
pit_status: PARTIAL — common lags are imposed, but source definitions and vintage histories cannot be identical across 452 claims.
native_result: Sixty-five percent fail the 1.96 hurdle and 82% fail the 2.78 multiple-testing hurdle; surviving magnitudes are much smaller than originally reported.
costs_capacity: Value weighting and microcap controls improve realism, but full spreads, borrow, impact, and capacity are absent.
replication_decay: Major independent replication; Chen-Zimmermann and Jensen-Kelly-Pedersen obtain higher rates under different definitions and benchmarks.
openness: Public paper, appendices, and author data library; raw CRSP/Compustat inputs require licenses.
key_limitation: A uniform replication protocol can depart materially from each original paper's exact estimand.

authors: Serhiy Kozak; Stefan Nagel; Shrihari Santosh
title: Shrinking the Cross-Section
target: Stochastic-discount-factor fit and cross-sectional expected-return performance
predictor_family: Large menus of characteristic-sorted equity portfolios
model_family: Bayesian and frequentist SDF shrinkage with economically motivated priors
sample_design: Cross-validation for penalty selection plus a pure out-of-sample exercise that fixes estimates before the later test period
benchmark: Unregularized high-dimensional SDFs and sparse conventional factor models
pit_status: PARTIAL — Portfolio formation follows published lag conventions; complete point-in-time accounting-database vintages are not the paper's central audit
native_result: Shrinking SDF coefficients toward economically plausible low-dimensional structure preserves substantial out-of-sample pricing and investment performance while limiting overfit
costs_capacity: The study focuses on pricing and SDF performance; turnover, shorting, impact, and capacity of the underlying characteristic portfolios are not fully netted
replication_decay: A fixed later-period test improves temporal credibility, but the evidence remains retrospective and is not independently live
openness: NBER and published versions are available; characteristic portfolio construction is documented, while raw CRSP and Compustat data are licensed
key_limitation: Cross-validation shares the historical regime, and economic implementability of a broad long-short factor menu is not established

authors: Markus Leippold; Qian Wang; Wenyu Zhou
title: Machine learning in the Chinese stock market
target: Cross-sectional stock returns
horizon: H3-H4: short and longer monthly horizons
predictor_family: Firm characteristics, liquidity, and ownership
model_family: Multiple machine-learning algorithms
sample_design: Chronological out-of-sample predictions compare algorithms across Chinese stocks, firm sizes, ownership, and forecast horizons.
benchmark: Linear characteristic models and U.S.-market predictor rankings
pit_status: PARTIAL — characteristics are lagged, but historical Chinese data revisions and investability screens are not fully frozen.
native_result: Liquidity is the leading predictor; retail presence strengthens small-stock short-horizon predictability, and large state-owned stocks remain predictable at longer horizons; OOS value survives transaction costs.
costs_capacity: Transaction costs are deducted in economic tests; price limits, short-sale constraints, impact, and capacity remain only partly represented.
replication_decay: External-market ML evidence supports nonlinear prediction, while the 2024 China anomaly replication shows most individual signals fail conservative tests.
openness: Verified DOI and documented algorithms; primary Chinese security data are proprietary.
key_limitation: China's retail dominance, state ownership, reforms, and trading constraints limit generalization and long-short executability.

authors: Andrew Y. Chen; Tom Zimmermann
title: Open Source Cross-Sectional Asset Pricing
target: Reproduced characteristic long-short returns
predictor_family: Three hundred nineteen cross-sectional predictors
model_family: Open standardized portfolio reconstruction
sample_design: Code and harmonized data definitions reconstruct 319 predictors and compare matched long-short t-statistics with original papers.
benchmark: Original reported t-statistics and Hou-Xue-Zhang replications
pit_status: PARTIAL — timing conventions are explicit, but vendor data are not a fully versioned point-in-time archive.
native_result: For 161 clearly significant original characteristics, 98% of reproductions exceed t=1.96; matched t-statistics have slope 0.88 and R-squared 82%.
costs_capacity: Gross long-short returns; implementation costs and capacity are not the replication target.
replication_decay: High computational reproduction contrasts with low rates from stricter standardized estimands, demonstrating design heterogeneity.
openness: Open code, definitions, derived signals, and documentation; licensed raw inputs remain required.
key_limitation: Reproducing original significance is not fresh-period validation or proof of cost-adjusted tradability.

authors: Alejandro Lopez-Lira; Yuehua Tang
title: Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models
venue: Journal of Financial Economics (forthcoming; earlier SSRN Working Paper 4412788)
target: Next-day individual-stock returns after news headlines
predictor_family: Company news headlines
model_family: ChatGPT sentiment prompts compared with earlier language models and vendor sentiment
sample_design: Daily headline classifications and long-short backtests centered on news after the model's stated training cutoff, with historical robustness exercises
benchmark: Commercial sentiment data, BERT-style models, GPT-1, GPT-2, and conventional news signals
pit_status: PARTIAL — Headlines are timestamped, but the closed model's training corpus, advertised cutoff, historical weights, and service updates are not independently auditable
native_result: ChatGPT headline scores predict next-day returns and initially outperform earlier language-model signals; revised tests show attenuation under costs and model variations
costs_capacity: Revised versions consider 10- and 25-basis-point trading costs, but daily turnover, spread heterogeneity, impact, shorting, API latency, and capacity remain material
replication_decay: Independent follow-up identifies company-knowledge distraction and long-horizon benchmark work reports substantial decay
openness: Working paper and prompt descriptions are public; headline feed, closed model weights, training corpus, and historical API snapshots are not
key_limitation: A claimed model knowledge cutoff is not a verifiable point-in-time training boundary, and the short post-cutoff sample has limited regime diversity

authors: Theis Ingerslev Jensen; Bryan T. Kelly; Lasse Heje Pedersen
title: Is There a Replication Crisis in Finance?
target: Factor returns, CAPM alphas, and replication probabilities
predictor_family: One hundred fifty-three characteristic factors
model_family: Standardized global factors and hierarchical Bayesian multiple testing
sample_design: A new open global panel builds 153 factors across 93 countries and tests U.S., temporal, and international replication under common construction.
benchmark: Hou-Xue-Zhang replication rate, CAPM alpha, and frequentist multiplicity correction
pit_status: PARTIAL — lags and nonmicrocap breakpoints are standardized; historical vendor vintages are incomplete.
native_result: The reported CAPM-alpha and Bayesian replication rate is 82.4%; the Bayesian false-discovery rate is 0.1%, and factors cluster into 13 themes that work globally.
costs_capacity: Nano stocks are excluded and weights capped, but realized spreads, borrow, impact, and capacity are not fully applied.
replication_decay: Directly disputes low replication-rate studies; differences trace to factor definitions, alpha versus raw return, weighting, and Bayesian pooling.
openness: Open factor data, documentation, and code-linked WRDS resource; security-level licensed inputs are still needed.
key_limitation: International observations are correlated and the hierarchical prior materially affects the replication conclusion.

authors: Doron Avramov; Si Cheng; Lior Metzker
title: Machine Learning vs. Economic Restrictions: Evidence from Stock Return Predictability
target: Cross-sectional stock returns and strategy performance
predictor_family: Firm characteristics and limits-to-arbitrage states
model_family: Deep learning and economically restricted portfolios
sample_design: Chronological out-of-sample tests examine microcap exclusions, distress, volatility states, long-only constraints, and recent subsamples.
benchmark: Unrestricted ML, anomaly portfolios, and economically filtered ML
pit_status: PARTIAL — characteristics are lagged; the feature set and restrictions are selected using broad historical knowledge.
native_result: ML profits concentrate in difficult-to-arbitrage stocks and high-volatility states; excluding them and adding reasonable costs materially attenuate performance, though recent long-only signals remain profitable.
costs_capacity: Reasonable trading costs, turnover, long-only positions, and exclusions are analyzed; full nonlinear impact and capacity are not.
replication_decay: Provides a direct implementation challenge to large gross ML gains; later real-time studies find smaller but sometimes positive cost-adjusted returns under modeled assumptions.
openness: Verified DOI with online data files and appendix; licensed source data remain necessary.
key_limitation: Cost assumptions are modeled, and surviving profitability is concentrated in specific constraints and eras.

authors: Nusret Cakici; Christian Fieberg; Daniel Metko; Adam Zaremba
title: Predicting Returns with Machine Learning across Horizons, Firm Size, and Time
venue: The Journal of Financial Data Science 5(4): 119-144
target: Cross-sectional stock returns at multiple forecast horizons
predictor_family: Firm characteristics and historical returns
model_family: Tree-based, neural, ensemble, and regularized machine-learning forecasts
sample_design: Chronological out-of-sample comparisons stratified by forecast horizon, firm size, and early versus recent market periods
benchmark: Traditional linear predictors, simple portfolio rules, and the same ML models across size and time strata
pit_status: PARTIAL — Tests are ordered out of sample as reported; close-price implementation timing and complete database-vintage reconstruction remain concerns
native_result: ML works best for short horizons, small firms, and early history, but annual forecasts fail to produce substantial economic gains for most of the U.S. market during the last two decades
costs_capacity: Economic portfolios are studied, but a complete institutional spread, impact, shorting, and capacity model is not established for the strongest small-stock signals
replication_decay: The paper directly documents decay across time, horizon, and market capitalization, challenging broad headline claims from pooled samples
openness: Published article and working-paper version are public; standard U.S. equity source databases are licensed
key_limitation: Subgroup analysis reduces effective sample size, while omitted implementation frictions are largest exactly where predictability is strongest

authors: Paul Glasserman; Caden Lin
title: Assessing Look-Ahead Bias in Stock Return Predictions Generated by GPT Sentiment Analysis
venue: The Journal of Financial Data Science 6(1): 25-42
target: News-sentiment trading returns inside and after GPT training windows
predictor_family: Original and company-anonymized financial news headlines
model_family: GPT sentiment classification with an anonymization debiasing test
sample_design: Trading signals from original headlines are compared with signals after removing company identifiers, separately inside and outside the model's training window
benchmark: Original-headline GPT strategy, anonymized-headline GPT strategy, and random replacement controls
pit_status: PARTIAL — Anonymization directly probes contamination, but the closed model's actual training documents and version history remain unknowable
native_result: Anonymized headlines outperform original headlines in-sample, implying that distraction from company knowledge can exceed direct look-ahead; out-of-sample look-ahead falls but distraction can persist
costs_capacity: The design isolates bias in a common signal; it does not provide a complete spread, turnover, impact, borrow, and capacity audit
replication_decay: This is an external methodological audit of GPT news strategies and explains why headline effects can change after decontamination
openness: Published article describes the anonymization method; closed-model weights and training data remain unavailable
key_limitation: Anonymization diagnoses but cannot fully identify all memorized future facts or changing API behavior

authors: Luyang Chen; Markus Pelger; Jason Zhu
title: Deep Learning in Asset Pricing
target: Conditional stock returns, SDF Sharpe ratio, and pricing errors
predictor_family: Firm characteristics and macroeconomic states
model_family: Adversarial deep neural stochastic-discount-factor model
sample_design: Chronological training and validation estimate a no-arbitrage neural SDF and compare held-out portfolio and pricing performance with linear and ML benchmarks.
benchmark: Linear factor models, PCA/IPCA, and alternative machine-learning SDFs
pit_status: PARTIAL — characteristics and macro inputs are lagged; final-vintage macro data and an ex-post feature menu remain.
native_result: The deep model outperforms all reported benchmarks out of sample in Sharpe ratio, explained variation, and pricing errors, while identifying nonlinear characteristic interactions.
costs_capacity: SDF and test portfolios are gross; turnover, leverage, impact, borrow, and capacity are not jointly constrained.
replication_decay: Publisher supplements support reproduction, but independent locked or prospective validation is not yet established.
openness: Publisher online appendix and data materials are linked; core CRSP/Compustat data are licensed.
key_limitation: A flexible adversarial model can exploit a repeatedly studied historical test set without demonstrating executable cost-adjusted alpha.

authors: Zhibing Li; Laura Xiaolei Liu; Xiaoyu Liu; K.C. John Wei
title: Replicating and Digesting Anomalies in the Chinese A-Share Market
target: Characteristic-portfolio raw returns and factor alphas
predictor_family: Four hundred sixty-nine anomaly variables
model_family: Standardized portfolio replication and factor spanning
sample_design: Mainboard breakpoints and value-weighted quintiles replicate 469 variables; raw, CAPM, three-factor, and post-2007 tests are reported.
benchmark: Zero spread, CAPM, Fama-French three-factor, CH3, CH4, and q-factor models
pit_status: PARTIAL — accounting lags are specified, but Chinese historical database revisions are not a frozen vintage archive.
native_result: Failure rates are 83.37% for raw spreads, 84.22% for CAPM alphas, and 86.99% for three-factor alphas; microcap-heavy conventional procedures have little capacity.
costs_capacity: Value weighting and mainboard breakpoints expose microcap capacity problems; full spreads, limits, impact, and shorting costs remain incomplete.
replication_decay: Fresh-market replication strongly supports conservative anomaly skepticism outside the United States.
openness: Publisher online appendix and data are linked at the verified DOI.
key_limitation: China's short-sale constraints, reforms, state ownership, and accounting shifts make long-short tests only partly executable.

authors: Bryan T. Kelly; Boris Kuznetsov; Semyon Malamud; Teng Andrea Xu
title: Artificial Intelligence Asset Pricing Models
geography_market: NYSE, AMEX, and NASDAQ, United States
target: SDF portfolio return and anomaly-factor pricing errors
predictor_family: One hundred thirty-two stock characteristics with cross-asset information sharing
model_family: Linear and deep nonlinear portfolio transformers
sample_design: Monthly 1963-2022 data use rolling 60-month training and one-month-ahead forecasts from 1968-2022, with post-2002 results reported separately.
benchmark: FF6, HXZ, SY, DHS, linear characteristic, random-feature, and multilayer-perceptron SDFs
pit_status: PARTIAL — characteristics are lagged, but the 132-feature library and test history are ex-post known and source vintages are incomplete.
native_result: The transformer reports out-of-sample Sharpe 4.57 and pricing error 0.09 versus 4.31 and 0.13 for the MLP; post-2002 values remain 3.37 and 0.34.
costs_capacity: Gross unconstrained SDF portfolios omit realized spreads, impact, leverage limits, borrow, financing, and capacity.
replication_decay: Cutoff-current working-paper evidence with no independent reproduction, sealed holdout, or prospective record.
openness: Open NBER paper and open JKP factor documentation; no complete independent code-and-environment archive identified.
key_limitation: Extremely parameterized costless portfolios and a repeatedly studied retrospective test can overstate executable performance.

authors: Weixian Waylon Li; Hyeonjun Kim; Mihai Cucuringu; Tiejun Ma
title: Can LLM-based Financial Investing Strategies Outperform the Market in Long Run?
venue: arXiv:2505.07078; accepted to KDD 2026 after the review cutoff
geography_market: United States, more than 100 stocks with historical index membership
target: Long-run portfolio return, risk, and drawdown from LLM-generated investment decisions
horizon: Daily decisions over roughly twenty years (H2-H6)
predictor_family: Price, fundamentals, news, and LLM-generated analysis
model_family: LLM agents compared with quantitative rules, machine learning, and reinforcement learning
sample_design: FINSABER backtests more than twenty years of multi-source data, historical constituents, delistings, multiple market regimes, and standardized commissions
benchmark: Buy-and-hold, index exposure, technical rules, ARIMA, XGBoost, and reinforcement-learning agents
pit_status: PARTIAL — Market inputs are aligned and survivorship controls are explicit, but historical prompts can overlap opaque LLM pretraining and are not equivalent to archived model versions
native_result: LLM strategies' reported advantages deteriorate over long samples: agents are overly conservative in bull markets, aggressive in bear markets, and generally fail to beat passive benchmarks consistently
costs_capacity: The simulator charges U.S. commissions of $0.0049 per share with a $0.99 minimum; spread, impact, borrow, API cost, latency, and capacity remain incomplete
replication_decay: The broad reimplementation contrasts with short-sample positive LLM studies, but it remains a retrospective benchmark rather than capital-at-risk live evidence
openness: Paper, FINSABER framework, and project resources are public; some underlying news and model APIs are vendor dependent
key_limitation: Opaque model training histories make strict historical point-in-time LLM evaluation impossible without chronologically frozen checkpoints

authors: Bin Li; Alberto G. Rossi; Xuemin Sterling Yan; Lingling Zheng
title: Machine learning from a “Universe” of signals: The role of feature engineering
target: One-month stock returns and long-short portfolio returns
predictor_family: More than 18,000 mechanically generated fundamental and past-return signals
model_family: Boosted regression trees, neural networks, and recursive ranking
sample_design: Training and validation precede a 1987-2019 chronological test; uncurated point-in-time-feasible signal universes are compared with published curated features.
benchmark: Gu-Kelly-Xiu and other curated-feature ML strategies; simple recursive signal ranking
pit_status: PIT — the broad signal universe is built from information available at each origin without assuming later anomaly discoveries were known.
native_result: Retrospective point-in-time-feasible ML is significantly positive but far weaker than curated-feature results; simple recursive ranking performs better, fundamental-signal cost-adjusted returns under the paper’s spread assumptions remain positive, and past-return-signal cost-adjusted returns are negative.
costs_capacity: Chen-Velikov spread estimates are deducted; market impact, borrow, financing, and capacity are not fully modeled.
replication_decay: Directly attenuates classic ML magnitudes by removing feature-publication look-ahead while preserving smaller positive fundamental-signal evidence.
openness: Verified DOI and referenced replication package; raw CRSP/Compustat data require licenses.
key_limitation: Mechanically generated ratios still embed researcher choices and the 1987-2019 test is retrospective rather than prospective.

authors: Mao Guan; Qian Chen
title: Leakage-Aware Benchmarking of LLM Forecasting: Real-Time Nowcasts as the Decision-Time Input for Macro Factor Ranking
venue: arXiv; ICML 2026 Workshop on AI Forecasting
target: Cross-sectional rank of next-month market-adjusted factor returns
predictor_family: Lagged macro data, archived inflation nowcasts, macro events, and historical analogs
model_family: Retrieval-augmented Qwen2.5-7B actor-critic
sample_design: Thirty-six monthly walk-forward decisions from April 2023 through March 2026 use lag-shifted FRED data, archived Cleveland Fed nowcasts, a twelve-month retrieval embargo, deterministic LLM outputs, ablations, and non-LLM baselines.
benchmark: Zero-shot LLM, raw retrieval, ridge models, and a k-nearest-neighbor macro-analog model under the same decision-time information set
pit_status: PARTIAL — market and macro inputs are origin-clean, but the open model's exact pretraining corpus is not a dated PIT archive
native_result: The full pipeline has mean rank IC 0.131, median 0.154, bootstrap 95% interval -0.02 to 0.28, and permutation p-value 0.11; k-nearest-neighbor analogs recover a slightly higher median IC of 0.161.
costs_capacity: A five-basis-point turnover charge appears only in a long-short sanity check explicitly described as non-deployable; impact, borrow, financing, and capacity are not validated.
replication_decay: Cutoff-current PIT design links the vintage-data and LLM-leakage literatures; no independent replication or prospective forecast archive exists by 2026-07-14.
openness: Open arXiv paper; authors release the 36 critic rules, parsed nowcast archive, representative cases, and walk-forward harness.
key_limitation: Only 36 months and seven factors are evaluated; the mean effect is underpowered, the k-nearest-neighbor benchmark explains much of the median signal, and model-pretraining contamination is not fully ruled out.

authors: Miquel Noguer i Alonso; Rodolfo Pereira Franklin
title: Pretrained Time-Series Foundation Models for Financial Return Forecasting
geography_market: Five liquid U.S. stocks: AAPL, AMZN, GOOG, JPM, and META
target: Twenty-day daily-return paths
predictor_family: Lagged univariate daily returns
model_family: Chronos, Moirai, TimesFM, and task-trained neural forecasting baselines
sample_design: Training history from September 2014 to August 2024 followed by ten rolling-origin 20-day windows through February 2026
benchmark: Gaussian random walk plus iTransformer, PatchTST, LSTM, and related trained neural baselines
pit_status: PARTIAL — Rolling-origin market data are ordered correctly; complete disjointness from every foundation model's pretraining corpus is not proven
native_result: Foundation models win many average rank comparisons, yet only isolated stock-model pairs significantly beat the random walk and iTransformer wins the META task
costs_capacity: No portfolio, spread, turnover, impact, or capacity test is provided
replication_decay: Ten later windows show weak and unstable significance; the study is small and not independently replicated
openness: Preprint and open checkpoints are available; the exact reproducibility package was not verified
key_limitation: Five stocks and ten short windows provide low power, and forecast loss is not translated into economic utility

authors: Tim Loughran; Bill McDonald
title: When Is a Liability Not a Liability? Textual Analysis, Dictionaries, and 10-Ks
target: Filing-period returns, volatility, trading volume, fraud, material weakness, and filing tone
predictor_family: 10-K text and finance-specific dictionaries
model_family: Domain dictionary counts and document-level regressions
sample_design: Large SEC 10-K corpus with event studies, cross-sectional regressions, and alternative word lists
benchmark: Harvard psychosociological dictionary and standard filing controls
pit_status: NOT-PIT — SEC filing dates anchor availability, but dictionary construction and hypothesis testing share the historical corpus
native_result: Almost three quarters of words classified as negative by the Harvard list are not negative in financial context; finance-specific lists better relate filing tone to market and firm outcomes
costs_capacity: The contribution is measurement validity, not a cost-adjusted trading strategy; execution costs and capacity are not tested.
replication_decay: The word lists became broad external benchmarks, while the original return associations remain retrospective
openness: The dictionaries and SEC filings are public; exact cleaned corpus construction requires substantial processing
key_limitation: Better domain measurement does not by itself establish incremental out-of-sample return forecasting

authors: Spyros Makridakis; Evangelos Spiliotis; Ross Hollyman; Fotios Petropoulos; Norman Swanson; Anil Gaba
title: The M6 forecasting competition: Bridging the gap between forecasting and investment decisions
geography_market: Fifty U.S. stocks and fifty global ETFs
target: Four-week cross-sectional return-rank probabilities and portfolio performance
horizon: Four weeks at each of twelve consecutive submission points (H3)
predictor_family: Unrestricted participant-selected market, fundamental, and alternative inputs
model_family: Open-method forecasting and portfolio competition
sample_design: Twelve prospective rolling submission rounds from February 2022 over approximately one year, covering 100 publicly tradable assets
benchmark: Competition forecasting score, standardized investment score, and simple benchmark submissions
pit_status: PIT — Forecasts and portfolios were frozen before each realized evaluation window; participants could learn between rounds
native_result: Only 23.3% of teams beat the forecasting benchmark, 28.8% beat the investment benchmark, and 6.7% beat both; forecasting rank explained only about 9.9% of investment rank variation
costs_capacity: Assets were tradable and portfolios risk constrained, but scores used hypothetical portfolios without realized fills, market impact, taxes, or capital deployment
replication_decay: Twelve prospective rounds provide repeated live-paper evidence; adaptive feedback and the short 2022-2023 regime limit independence
openness: Competition rules, assets, submissions, and outcome summaries are public
key_limitation: One volatile year, public-leaderboard adaptation, and hypothetical execution prevent a LIVE-X interpretation

authors: Songrun He; Linying Lv; Asaf Manela; Jimmy Wu
title: Chronologically Consistent Large Language Models
target: Language-task accuracy and next-day stock returns from financial news
horizon: Annual model vintages and next-day returns (H2)
predictor_family: Timestamped pre-forecast text corpora and financial news
model_family: ChronoBERT and ChronoGPT checkpoints trained separately for each historical year
sample_design: Year-specific models from 1999 onward train only on text available by each cutoff; real-time embeddings are compared with standard models on NLP and asset-pricing tasks
benchmark: BERT, FinBERT, StoriesLM, larger open-weight LLMs, and state-of-the-art news-return models
pit_status: PARTIAL — The model suite is explicitly trained on timestamped corpora truncated at each year, substantially reducing pretraining look-ahead
native_result: Chronologically clean models match or outperform prior leak-free NLP models and produce next-day news-return Sharpe ratios comparable to state-of-the-art models, suggesting modest leakage effects in this application
costs_capacity: The asset-pricing exercise does not provide a complete executable cost, turnover, impact, borrow, and capacity analysis
replication_decay: Leakage is evaluated through controlled vintage models, but model construction and the finance test are from the same team and not live
openness: ChronoBERT checkpoints are released on Hugging Face and the timestamped-corpus method is documented
key_limitation: Corpus timestamps do not guarantee that every source was available identically in real time, and comparable Sharpe is not an after-cost trading edge.

authors: Yahui Bai; Yuhe Gao; Runzhe Wan; Sheng Zhang; Rui Song
title: A Review of Reinforcement Learning in Financial Applications
venue: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application 12: 209-232
asset_class: Equities, derivatives, foreign exchange, and portfolio applications
target: Trading, portfolio allocation, market making, execution, and financial decision performance
predictor_family: Market states, order books, prices, and portfolio variables across surveyed studies
model_family: Value-based, policy-gradient, actor-critic, multi-agent, and model-based reinforcement learning
sample_design: Review and meta-analysis of reinforcement-learning applications in trading, portfolio allocation, market making, execution, and other financial decisions.
benchmark: Traditional optimization, supervised ML, rule-based strategies, and within-paper baselines
pit_status: PARTIAL — The review inherits heterogeneous and often incomplete point-in-time controls from its source studies
native_result: Meta-analysis identifies factors associated with reported RL performance while concluding that robustness, MDP design, explainability, and common benchmarking remain major barriers
costs_capacity: Treatment of transaction costs, impact, and capacity varies widely across underlying studies and is not harmonized
replication_decay: Cross-paper synthesis reveals heterogeneity rather than a single stable effect; publication and benchmark-selection bias remain possible
openness: Peer-reviewed review and references are accessible; no fully executable standardized corpus is supplied.
key_limitation: Incomparable tasks, rewards, data splits, and cost assumptions prevent a clean pooled estimate of deployable RL alpha

authors: Tim Bollerslev; Benjamin Hood; John Huss; Lasse Heje Pedersen
title: Risk Everywhere: Modeling and Managing Volatility
asset_class: Equities, equity indexes, government bonds, currencies, and commodities
target: Next-period realized volatility and volatility-managed portfolio weights
predictor_family: High-frequency realized variation and cross-asset volatility information
model_family: Cross-asset volatility forecast combinations and dynamic risk scaling
sample_design: More than 50 liquid assets over more than two decades, with out-of-sample forecast and portfolio comparisons
benchmark: Asset-specific volatility forecasts, static volatility targeting, and conventional risk models
pit_status: PARTIAL — Intraday observations are time ordered; exchange microstructure and vendor-history revisions are not independently replayed
native_result: Pooling risk signals across markets improves volatility forecasts and produces sizable risk-adjusted and utility gains over asset-by-asset methods
costs_capacity: Turnover and a 48-basis-point annual switching-cost threshold are discussed, but nonlinear market impact and crisis-time capacity are not fully simulated
replication_decay: The effect appears across many asset classes in one integrated study; no independent live execution record is supplied
openness: Published paper and appendices are public; high-frequency source data are largely licensed
key_limitation: Forecast gains are converted to friction-limited portfolio evidence under simplified execution assumptions

authors: Manapon Limkriangkrai; Daniel Chai; Gaoping Zheng
title: Market Intraday Momentum: APAC Evidence
geography_market: China, Hong Kong SAR, Japan, Singapore, and South Korea
target: Last-half-hour ETF return
predictor_family: First-half-hour return, volatility, and trading volume
model_family: Intraday predictive regressions
sample_design: Direct external-market application of the U.S. intraday-momentum design across five APAC ETF markets, including COVID-period stability checks.
benchmark: Gao-Han-Li-Zhou U.S. intraday-momentum effect
pit_status: PIT—first-half-hour information precedes the close-period target
native_result: Forecast result: intraday momentum is evident mainly in China and Japan, weak in South Korea, absent in Hong Kong and Singapore, and weaker during COVID where present. After-cost trading P&L is not established.
costs_capacity: No fully specified cross-market after-cost strategy; ETF liquidity differences are material.
replication_decay: Provides direct external heterogeneity and rejects a universal-market interpretation of the original U.S. result.
openness: Verified article link and public metadata; intraday market data are not bundled.
key_limitation: ETF liquidity and trading-hour structures differ materially across countries, and executable returns after costs are not reported.

authors: Paul C. Tetlock
title: Giving Content to Investor Sentiment: The Role of Media in the Stock Market
target: Daily aggregate stock returns, trading volume, and subsequent reversal
predictor_family: Dictionary-based pessimism in the Wall Street Journal's Abreast of the Market column
model_family: Principal-component text score with vector autoregression and event regressions
sample_design: Daily newspaper text matched to market outcomes with contemporaneous controls and predictive lag tests
benchmark: Lagged market returns, volume, and standard sentiment controls
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Articles precede measured returns, but vocabulary and specifications are evaluated on the same historical sample rather than a frozen holdout
native_result: High media pessimism predicts short-run downward market pressure followed by reversal and unusually high trading volume
costs_capacity: No implementable portfolio with release latency, spread, market impact, or transaction costs is evaluated
replication_decay: The result founded a large text-finance literature, but this paper itself has no out-of-sample or prospective test
openness: Published article is available; historical Wall Street Journal text requires licensed access
key_limitation: Same-sample language construction and aggregate regressions support association, not a deployable forecast

authors: Graham Elliott; Antonio Gargano; Allan Timmermann
title: Complete Subset Regressions
target: U.S. equity premium
predictor_family: Twelve macro-financial predictors
model_family: Complete-subset regression forecast combinations with recursive subset-size selection
sample_design: Quarterly 1947Q1-2010Q4 data with recursive pseudo-out-of-sample forecasts and subset size selected using prior forecast errors
benchmark: Historical-average forecast and unrestricted predictive regression
pit_status: PARTIAL — Forecast ordering and tuning are recursive; the macro inputs are not a full real-time-vintage reconstruction
native_result: Selected complete-subset forecasts reduce out-of-sample squared error and yield portfolio utility gains relative to the historical average
costs_capacity: The paper evaluates forecast and allocation value but does not provide a full turnover, slippage, leverage, and financing audit
replication_decay: Multiple recursive windows support within-sample robustness; the evidence is not a prospective or independent live replication
openness: Published article and working-paper versions are available; core predictors are standard, though exact vintages require reconstruction
key_limitation: The method is tested mainly on one low-frequency aggregate series, and subset selection still searches across many correlated models

authors: Tobias Preis; Helen Susannah Moat; H. Eugene Stanley
title: Quantifying Trading Behavior in Financial Markets Using Google Trends
geography_market: United States, Dow Jones Industrial Average
target: Next-week market direction and strategy return
predictor_family: Google Trends search-volume indices for finance-related terms
model_family: Threshold trading rules
sample_design: Weekly Google Trends series and DJIA backtests with comparisons across 98 search terms
benchmark: Buy-and-hold and random or nonfinancial search-term strategies
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Trading uses prior weekly search changes, but downloaded historical Google Trends values are normalized and can be revised; terms and thresholds were not frozen before an independent holdout
native_result: A debt-search strategy reports large cumulative gains and higher risk-adjusted performance than buy-and-hold, while many semantically unrelated terms also generate apparent signals
costs_capacity: Weekly trading limits raw turnover, but spreads, slippage, taxes, and model-selection costs are not comprehensively deducted
replication_decay: A direct reanalysis later showed sensitivity to keyword selection and unstable Google data vintages
openness: Article and Google Trends interface are public; exact historical query output is not permanently versioned
key_limitation: Same-sample term search and mutable normalized data create severe data-snooping and reproducibility risks

authors: Damien Challet; Ahmed Bel Hadj Ayed
title: Predicting Financial Markets with Google Trends and Not So Random Keywords
geography_market: United States, Dow Jones Industrial Average
target: Next-week strategy return
predictor_family: Google Trends search-volume indices across finance and unrelated term lists
model_family: Replicated threshold rules with systematic keyword testing
sample_design: Direct reproduction and expansion of the Preis-Moat-Stanley strategy across many keyword lists and repeated Google Trends downloads
benchmark: Original debt-keyword rule, random and semantically unrelated keywords, and buy-and-hold
pit_status: NOT-PIT — The audit shows that historical Google Trends values can change between downloads, so an immutable point-in-time feature history is unavailable
native_result: Comparable apparent performance arises from unrelated keywords and favorable term selection; instability of downloaded data further weakens the original broad forecasting claim
costs_capacity: The core failure occurs before execution; weekly costs and slippage would further reduce marginal strategies
replication_decay: This direct external reanalysis documents specification and data-vintage fragility rather than stable replication
openness: Preprint and keyword tests are public; Google Trends does not provide a permanently frozen historical database
key_limitation: The audit cannot reconstruct the exact original query vintages, which is itself the central reproducibility problem

authors: Bevan J. Blair; Ser-Huang Poon; Stephen J. Taylor
title: Forecasting S&P 100 Volatility: The Incremental Information Content of Implied Volatilities and High-Frequency Index Returns
target: Realized S&P 100 volatility
predictor_family: VIX, daily index returns, and 5-minute realized variation
model_family: ARCH-family forecast combinations and encompassing comparisons
sample_design: Fixed estimation period 1987-01-02 through 1992-12-31 and fixed out-of-sample evaluation from 1993-01-04 through 1999-12-31.
benchmark: ARCH forecasts from daily and 5-minute returns
pit_status: PIT—VIX and return inputs are available before each target period
native_result: Forecast accuracy: VIX is most accurate for every tested horizon and performance measure; intraday returns add no significant incremental information. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No volatility-trading or hedging decision mapping; data and model requirements are modest.
replication_decay: Later cross-asset work confirms that implied volatility adds information beyond realized components, while the strength varies by market.
openness: Verified article link and public manuscript copies; source data and code are not packaged.
key_limitation: The result predates the modern VIX methodology and covers one U.S. index.

authors: Tim Bollerslev; George Tauchen; Hao Zhou
title: Expected Stock Returns and Variance Risk Premia
target: Aggregate excess stock-market return
horizon: H3-H4—one month through two years, strongest near one quarter
predictor_family: Model-free implied variance minus high-frequency realized variance
model_family: Overlapping predictive regressions motivated by equilibrium theory
sample_design: Monthly observations from January 1990 through December 2007 with Hodrick-style overlap-robust inference across forecast horizons.
benchmark: P/E ratio, default spread, consumption-wealth ratio, and implied or realized variance alone
pit_status: PIT—option variance and realized variance are formed before the return horizon; macro controls use the most recently available observation
native_result: Forecast accuracy: quarterly VRP regression has adjusted R² 6.82% and t=2.86, with the strongest pattern at the quarterly horizon. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No investable timing rule, turnover, transaction costs, drawdown, or capacity analysis.
replication_decay: International follow-up finds similar horizon patterns across seven additional countries and stronger global-VRP panel results.
openness: Public paper copies and formulae are available; option and intraday datasets are proprietary.
key_limitation: Short post-1990 sample, overlapping returns, and an in-sample horizon search make the large R² unsuitable as a live P&L claim.

authors: Ian Martin
title: What Is the Expected Return on the Market?
target: Conditional market equity premium and crash probability
predictor_family: Option-implied risk-neutral variance summarized by SVIX
model_family: No-arbitrage lower bound plus predictive regressions
sample_design: OptionMetrics SPX surfaces from 1996-01-04 through 2012-01-31; theoretical lower bounds are compared with subsequently realized market returns at five horizons.
benchmark: Constant or conventional average equity premium; unrestricted predictive intercept and slope
pit_status: PIT—SVIX uses option prices observable at each horizon's origin
native_result: Forecast result: the lower bound averages about 5%, exceeds 20% in the 2008 crisis, and the joint restriction intercept=0 and slope=1 is not rejected at any horizon. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No timing-strategy costs or capacity; proposed simple variance swaps still require tradable quotes and collateral.
replication_decay: The option-implied expected-return literature expands this bound to stocks and alternative tail measures, but prospective validation remains absent.
openness: Public manuscript and bibliographic record; OptionMetrics inputs are proprietary.
key_limitation: Failure to reject tightness is not an equivalence test, and the sample contains only a small number of crisis episodes.

authors: Turan G. Bali; Heiner Beckmeyer; Mathis Moerke; Florian Weigert
title: Option Return Predictability with Machine Learning and Big Data
target: Next-month delta-hedged and raw option returns
predictor_family: Option, underlying-stock, and macro characteristics
model_family: Neural networks, random forests, gradient boosting, and penalized regressions
sample_design: Approximately twelve million option-month observations from 1996-2020, with a 2003-2020 rolling out-of-sample test
benchmark: Linear, shrinkage, dimension-reduction, and standard option-characteristic models
pit_status: PARTIAL — Predictors are lagged and tests are chronological; quote availability, stale quotes, and complete vendor-vintage histories are not replayed order by order
native_result: Machine-learning forecasts produce sizable out-of-sample long-short spreads; nonlinear interactions materially outperform linear approaches
costs_capacity: The paper applies 25%-100% effective-spread cost scenarios, delta-hedging costs, and robustness filters; fills, margin funding, impact, and portfolio capacity remain approximate
replication_decay: Later holdouts and severe spread haircuts retain positive results in the same database; independent live options execution is absent
openness: Authors provide code with pseudo-data; OptionMetrics and CRSP inputs are licensed
key_limitation: Quoted-spread haircuts do not reproduce executable size, queueing, hedging slippage, margin, or crowded short-option capacity

authors: Bent Jesper Christensen; Nagpurnanand R. Prabhala
title: The Relation Between Implied and Realized Volatility
target: Realized index volatility over the option horizon
predictor_family: At-the-money option-implied volatility and lagged realized volatility
model_family: Predictive encompassing regressions
sample_design: Nonoverlapping monthly observations over 1983-1995, with explicit analysis of the October 1987 regime break.
benchmark: Past realized volatility
pit_status: PIT—option quotes and historical volatility are observed at the forecast origin
native_result: Forecast accuracy: implied volatility outperforms past volatility and subsumes it in some specifications; apparent bias is strongly regime-dependent around the 1987 crash. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No options strategy, spread, hedging-cost, or capacity analysis.
replication_decay: Later fixed-holdout and multi-asset studies broadly confirm incremental implied-volatility information but not universal unbiasedness.
openness: Verified DOI and public metadata; raw option data and code are not open.
key_limitation: A single index, low monthly sample size, and a major regime break make the unbiasedness conclusion unstable.

authors: George J. Jiang; Yisong S. Tian
title: The Model-Free Implied Volatility and Its Information Content
target: Future realized volatility over the option horizon
predictor_family: Cross-strike model-free option-implied variance
model_family: Model-free variance integration with predictive encompassing tests
sample_design: SPX option surfaces are integrated across strikes under a jump-compatible model-free construction and compared with Black-Scholes IV and past realized volatility.
benchmark: Black-Scholes implied volatility and lagged realized volatility
pit_status: PIT—uses contemporaneously observable option quotes to forecast later realized volatility
native_result: Forecast accuracy: model-free IV subsumes the information in Black-Scholes IV and past realized volatility and is the more efficient forecast. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No executable variance-trade result; dense strike coverage and quote cleaning create implementation demands.
replication_decay: Model-free implied variance became the standard basis for VIX and variance-risk-premium work; later studies extend it across markets.
openness: Verified bibliographic page and public manuscript versions; OptionMetrics/CBOE data are licensed.
key_limitation: The predictive tests are retrospective and sensitive to option interpolation, strike truncation, and microstructure filters.

authors: Torben G. Andersen; Tim Bollerslev; Francis X. Diebold; Paul Labys
title: Modeling and Forecasting Realized Volatility
target: Daily realized volatility, covariance, return density, and return quantiles
predictor_family: High-frequency realized volatility and cross-market covariance
model_family: Long-memory Gaussian vector autoregression with lognormal-normal mixture density
sample_design: Nearly thirteen years of continuous quotes; 2,449 days from 1986-12-01 through 1996-12-01 for estimation and a fixed 596-day holdout from 1996-12-02 through 1999-06-30.
benchmark: Popular daily ARCH and related parametric volatility models
pit_status: PIT—holdout forecasts use only prior intraday returns
native_result: Forecast accuracy: the realized-volatility VAR performed strongly relative to daily ARCH models and produced well-calibrated density and quantile forecasts in the fixed holdout. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: Risk-forecasting evidence only; no trading costs or capital-capacity mapping.
replication_decay: The realized-volatility measurement and long-memory findings became foundational and were extended by HAR and multi-asset realized-measure studies.
openness: Published article and public copies are available; the underlying continuous quote data are not bundled with executable code.
key_limitation: Two highly liquid FX rates and an older market structure limit direct transfer to equities, options, and modern fragmented venues.

authors: Ailing Zeng; Muxi Chen; Lei Zhang; Qiang Xu
title: Are Transformers Effective for Time Series Forecasting?
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence 37(9): 11121-11128
asset_class: Foreign exchange plus nonfinancial benchmark time series
geography_market: Eight public exchange-rate series within a nine-dataset forecasting benchmark
target: Multistep time-series levels
horizon: Multiple medium and long sequence horizons (H3-H5)
predictor_family: Lagged multivariate time-series values
model_family: DLinear and NLinear linear baselines versus Transformer forecasters
sample_design: Standard chronological train, validation, and test splits on nine public datasets, including an exchange-rate benchmark
benchmark: Repeat-last-value, linear models, and leading Transformer architectures such as FEDformer
pit_status: PARTIAL — Chronological splits are used, but the public benchmarks have been repeatedly reused for architecture development
native_result: Simple one-layer linear models outperform sophisticated Transformer forecasters across the nine benchmark datasets; repeating the last value is especially hard to beat for exchange rates
costs_capacity: No trading strategy, turnover, spread, or capacity analysis is performed
replication_decay: The public code and data enabled extensive follow-up testing; later architectures improve some tasks but do not erase the need for naive and linear baselines
openness: Code and benchmark datasets are public
key_limitation: Level-forecast mean-squared error on reused benchmarks is not return prediction or investment performance

authors: Peter R. Hansen; Asger Lunde
title: A Forecast Comparison of Volatility Models: Does Anything Beat a GARCH(1,1)?
target: Daily conditional return variance
predictor_family: Lagged returns and asymmetric volatility dynamics
model_family: 330 ARCH/GARCH-family specifications
sample_design: Retrospective out-of-sample forecast comparison for DM/USD and IBM, using realized variance for IBM and data-snooping-aware SPA and Reality Check tests.
benchmark: GARCH(1,1), with ARCH(1) as a weak reference benchmark
pit_status: PIT—forecasts use lagged market observations
native_result: Forecast accuracy: no sophisticated model significantly beat GARCH(1,1) for DM/USD, while leverage-capable models clearly beat it for IBM. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No trading rule, transaction-cost model, impact estimate, or capacity analysis.
replication_decay: The hard-to-beat GARCH result persists as a baseline lesson, but later realized-volatility evidence shifts the leading benchmark toward HAR-type models and shows asset-specific heterogeneity.
openness: Public metadata and working-paper copies exist; estimation data and code are not supplied as a complete reproducibility package.
key_limitation: Only two return series are studied, and benchmark conclusions differ sharply between FX and equity.

authors: Fulvio Corsi
