title: A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility
geography_market: USD/CHF, S&P 500 futures, and 30-year U.S. Treasury-bond futures
target: Realized volatility
horizon: H2-H3—one day, one week, and two weeks
predictor_family: Daily, weekly, and monthly realized-volatility components
model_family: HAR-RV linear cascade model
sample_design: Long tick-data series beginning in 1989-1990; AR and HAR models are re-estimated daily on 1,000-observation rolling windows for retrospective out-of-sample forecasts.
benchmark: AR(1), AR(3), and ARFIMA(5,d,0)
pit_status: PIT — PARTIAL—HAR forecasts are point-in-time, but the ARFIMA comparator estimates its fractional-integration parameter on the full sample
native_result: Forecast accuracy: HAR(3) steadily beat short-memory AR models at all three horizons and performed similarly to ARFIMA. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No decision rule, transaction costs, impact, or capacity test; the linear model is computationally light.
replication_decay: HAR became the standard realized-volatility benchmark; large 2024 studies confirm that properly fitted HAR remains difficult for nonlinear ML to beat.
openness: Public article copies are available; the original tick datasets and an executable replication package are not bundled.
key_limitation: The strongest long-memory comparator is not fully out of sample because its d parameter uses the full series.

authors: Hanno Lustig; Nikolai Roussanov; Adrien Verdelhan
title: Common Risk Factors in Currency Markets
geography_market: Broad developed and emerging currency cross-section from a USD-investor perspective
target: One-month currency excess return from spot and forward rates, not spot appreciation alone
predictor_family: Forward discount/interest-rate carry
model_family: Characteristic-sorted portfolios, principal components, and linear factor pricing
sample_design: Monthly currency portfolios sorted by forward discounts; cross-sectional and time-series factor tests
benchmark: Dollar return factor and standard asset-pricing restrictions
pit_status: PIT — spot and one-month forward quotes are observable at portfolio formation
native_result: The HMLFX carry factor explained about 70% of variation in average returns across six carry portfolios; the high-minus-low spread remained about 4.8% annually after stated transaction costs.
costs_capacity: Bid-ask transaction costs were considered; financing beyond forward pricing, market impact, and crowded-position capacity were not.
replication_decay: Carry spreads recur across many samples, but crash exposure, changing covered-interest parity, and no frozen prospective test limit stability claims.
openness: Public NBER/author manuscripts are available; no verified complete production code.
key_limitation: The carry factor is formed from the test assets, so strong in-sample pricing does not constitute independent return forecasting.

authors: Lukas Menkhoff; Lucio Sarno; Maik Schmeling; Andreas Schrimpf
title: Carry Trades and Global Foreign Exchange Volatility
geography_market: Up to 48 developed and emerging currencies against the USD
target: One-month carry-trade currency excess return from spot and forward rates
predictor_family: Interest-rate carry and exposure to global FX-volatility innovations
model_family: Portfolio sorts and cross-sectional factor pricing
sample_design: Monthly November 1983-November 2008 spot/forward data with five carry portfolios and robustness samples
benchmark: Carry portfolios priced by conventional risk and liquidity factors
pit_status: PIT — forward discounts and realized market returns are dated; the risk explanation is estimated in-sample
native_result: Global FX-volatility risk captured more than 90% of the cross-sectional carry-return spread; high-rate currencies lost when volatility unexpectedly rose.
costs_capacity: Quoted transaction costs and liquidity risk were examined, but market impact, leverage funding, and crowded unwinds were not fully modeled.
replication_decay: Volatility/crash exposure is widely reproduced, while the magnitude of cost-adjusted carry returns varies strongly across crises and currency screens.
openness: Public author manuscript and stable publisher metadata are available; no verified code archive.
key_limitation: This is an in-sample risk explanation of realized carry-inclusive returns, not a locked forecast of future carry profitability.

authors: Lukas Menkhoff; Lucio Sarno; Maik Schmeling; Andreas Schrimpf
title: Currency Momentum Strategies
geography_market: Up to 48 developed and emerging currencies against the USD
target: Cross-sectional currency excess return from spot and forward rates, not spot return alone
horizon: H3; 1-12 month formation and holding variants
predictor_family: Cross-sectional momentum in past currency excess returns
model_family: Winner-minus-loser portfolio sorts and risk-factor regressions
sample_design: Monthly January 1976-January 2010 data with many formation/holding combinations and subperiod checks
benchmark: Carry, conventional risk factors, and technical-rule returns
pit_status: PIT — past spot/forward returns are observable at formation
native_result: Winner-minus-loser excess-return spreads reached about 10% annually gross and were distinct from carry; full quoted spreads reduced the best strategy to roughly 4%.
costs_capacity: Full and fractional quoted bid-ask spreads were tested; turnover exceeded 70% monthly for the fastest rule, and effective costs/capacity remain uncertain.
replication_decay: Later work confirms momentum links but shows substantial decay for broader technical-rule portfolios; no sealed test of the selected variant exists.
openness: Public BIS/author manuscripts are available; no verified full code/data package.
key_limitation: A large strategy grid and selecting the best formation/holding rule make the headline return vulnerable to search and turnover costs.

authors: Òscar Jordà; Alan M. Taylor
title: The Carry Trade and Fundamentals: Nothing to Fear but FEER Itself
target: One-month carry-trade excess return, explicitly including interest differentials and spot moves
predictor_family: Carry conditioned on fundamental-equilibrium-exchange-rate value and momentum
model_family: Threshold error-correction forecasts and binary-outcome classification
sample_design: Monthly January 1986-December 2008 panel; January 2004-December 2008 reserved for recursive out-of-sample evaluation
benchmark: Naive diversified carry trade and unconditioned forecasts
pit_status: PARTIAL — market inputs are dated, but FEER estimation uses macro data without full vintage reconstruction
native_result: The FEER-conditioned carry strategy improved return, volatility, and skewness and earned 3.64% annualized in the four-year window ending in 2008 when naive carry was negative.
costs_capacity: A 2 bp G10 round-trip cost stress caused only small reported reductions; impact, leverage constraints, and capacity were not modeled.
replication_decay: The crisis holdout is informative, but the exact FEER rule lacks independent frozen or prospective replication.
openness: Public NBER manuscript and journal metadata are available; no verified code package.
key_limitation: FEER construction and threshold choices create researcher degrees of freedom, and the out-of-sample window is only five years.

authors: Martin D. D. Evans; Richard K. Lyons
title: Order Flow and Exchange Rate Dynamics
target: Contemporaneous daily spot exchange-rate change; any reported forecast is not carry-inclusive
predictor_family: Signed interdealer order flow and dealer inventory
model_family: Microstructure regressions and recursive pseudo-forecast comparison
sample_design: Four-month May-August 1996 Reuters interdealer sample; daily USD/DEM specification reports R-squared above 60%
benchmark: Macro exchange-rate models and random walk
pit_status: NOT-PIT — for forecasting—the pseudo-forecasts use realized future order flow; contemporaneous regressions are correctly timed only as explanation
native_result: Order flow strongly explained concurrent spot changes, but the paper explicitly notes that its forecasts use future realized forcing variables and are not true out-of-sample forecasts.
costs_capacity: No executable strategy, spread, delay, impact, or capacity assessment.
replication_decay: Later studies with lagged, available order flow provide valid short-horizon forecasting evidence, but this record cannot support that predictive claim.
openness: Public BIS version and publisher metadata are available; proprietary underlying transactions are not open.
key_limitation: The influential explanatory result is often misread as forecasting; unavailable future order flow is a fatal timing defect for that interpretation.

authors: Richard A. Meese; Kenneth Rogoff
title: Empirical Exchange Rate Models of the Seventies: Do They Fit Out of Sample?
geography_market: USD/GBP, USD/DEM, USD/JPY, and trade-weighted USD
target: Nominal spot exchange-rate level/change, not a carry-inclusive currency return
predictor_family: Monetary, price, output, interest-rate, and current-account fundamentals
model_family: Structural monetary/current-account models and univariate time-series models
sample_design: Monthly March 1973-June 1981 data; recursively re-estimated forecasts from November 1976-June 1981
benchmark: Driftless random walk/no-change forecast
pit_status: NOT-PIT — forecasts were granted realized future explanatory variables
native_result: The random walk forecast performed at least as well as the estimated models at every reported 1-12 month horizon.
costs_capacity: Forecast-accuracy study; no trading costs, financing, impact, or capacity analysis.
replication_decay: The random-walk hurdle became the durable benchmark; later studies found only model-, horizon-, and period-specific exceptions.
openness: Publisher metadata and a public manuscript are available; no verified code package.
key_limitation: The short early-float sample is low-powered, and use of realized future fundamentals makes the negative result unusually favorable to structural models but non-real-time.

authors: Nelson C. Mark
title: Exchange Rates and Fundamentals: Evidence on Long-Horizon Predictability
geography_market: USD against CAD, DEM, JPY, and CHF
target: Multi-quarter nominal spot exchange-rate change, not carry-inclusive return
predictor_family: Deviation of spot exchange rates from monetary fundamental value
model_family: Long-horizon predictive regressions with bootstrap inference
sample_design: Quarterly 1973Q2-1991Q4 data; overlapping-horizon regressions and recursive out-of-sample point forecasts
benchmark: Driftless random walk
pit_status: PARTIAL — recursive forecasts, but revised macro data and a maintained long-run relation were used
native_result: Bias-adjusted slopes and R-squared values rose with horizon, and point forecasts generally beat the random walk at longer horizons.
costs_capacity: No conversion of spot forecast gains into cost-adjusted executable returns.
replication_decay: Kilian (1999) and Faust, Rogers, and Wright (2003) showed weak power, sample sensitivity, and strong data-vintage dependence.
openness: Stable journal/RePEc metadata are public; no verified original code package.
key_limitation: Overlapping long horizons, a very small effective sample, and sensitivity to cointegration and vintage choices weaken the original inference.

authors: Yin-Wong Cheung; Menzie D. Chinn; Antonio Garcia Pascual
title: Empirical Exchange Rate Models of the Nineties: Are Any Fit to Survive?
venue: Journal of International Money and Finance 24(7): 1150-1175
target: Nominal spot exchange-rate level/change and direction, not carry-inclusive return
predictor_family: PPP, monetary, interest-parity, productivity, and composite fundamentals
model_family: First-difference and error-correction forecasts with multiple loss criteria
sample_design: Recursive ex-ante forecasts with the cointegrating vector updated through time and multiple evaluation periods
benchmark: Random walk/no change
pit_status: PARTIAL — forecast equations were recursively updated, but real-time macro vintages were not reconstructed
native_result: No model consistently beat the random walk on MSE; some structural models predicted direction at long horizons, but winners changed by currency and period.
costs_capacity: No trading-cost, financing, or capacity analysis.
replication_decay: Confirms broad instability rather than a durable winner after the original Meese-Rogoff finding.
openness: Public author manuscript and stable publisher metadata are available; no verified code package.
key_limitation: Many model-currency-horizon comparisons create multiplicity, while directional significance does not establish economic value.

authors: Tanya Molodtsova; David H. Papell
title: Out-of-Sample Exchange Rate Predictability with Taylor Rule Fundamentals
geography_market: Twelve currencies against the USD in the post-Bretton Woods float
target: Future nominal spot exchange-rate change, not carry-inclusive return
horizon: H3-H4; 1 to 36 months, with strongest evidence at short horizons
predictor_family: Taylor-rule inflation, output-gap, interest-rate, and real-exchange-rate fundamentals
model_family: Recursive predictive regressions with Clark-West nested-model inference
sample_design: Retrospective recursive forecasts across 12 currencies and multiple Taylor-rule specifications
benchmark: Driftless random walk plus conventional PPP, monetary, and interest-differential models
pit_status: PARTIAL — recursive forecast timing, but revised macro series/output-gap estimates rather than a complete real-time vintage set
native_result: Short-run predictability was reported for 11 of 12 currencies, much more often for Taylor-rule fundamentals than for conventional models.
costs_capacity: Statistical forecast comparison only; no cost-adjusted trading or capacity result.
replication_decay: Ince, Molodtsova, and Papell (2016) extended the same lineage through 2014 with positive results; independence remains limited.
openness: The author page provides the paper, data, and a data appendix; no verified executable code archive.
key_limitation: Results span many output-gap and Taylor-rule variants, and the Clark-West rejection does not by itself quantify economically useful forecast improvement.

authors: Dagfinn Rime; Lucio Sarno; Elvira Sojli
title: Exchange Rate Forecasting, Order Flow and Macroeconomic Information
geography_market: Three major exchange rates from Reuters interdealer data
target: Next-day spot exchange-rate movement and associated allocation utility, not a long-horizon carry return
predictor_family: Lagged signed order flow and macroeconomic news/expectations
model_family: Recursive microstructure forecasting regressions and utility-based allocation
sample_design: One year of high-frequency data; first portion estimated models and June 15, 2004-February 14, 2005 was recursively forecast
benchmark: Random walk and alternative macro/flow models
pit_status: PIT — forecasts condition on order flow available by the daily forecast origin
native_result: Order-flow forecasts delivered Sharpe ratios around or above one and high performance fees relative to the random walk.
costs_capacity: Utility was evaluated, but realistic spread, latency, market impact, and capacity were not comprehensively deducted.
replication_decay: The result improves timing validity over Evans-Lyons, but the proprietary one-year sample has not been independently reproduced at equal quality.
openness: Public manuscript is available; the Reuters order-flow data and full replication package are not open.
key_limitation: Only three rates and about eight out-of-sample months make the economic result imprecise and highly dependent on proprietary flow coverage.

authors: Ron Jongen; Willem F. C. Verschoor; Christian C. P. Wolff
title: Foreign Exchange Rate Expectations: Survey and Synthesis
asset_class: FX—spot expectations and carry-inclusive forward-bias evidence
geography_market: International FX survey and microstructure literature
target: Survey spot-rate forecasts, forecast errors, and forward-discount excess returns
horizon: H3-H5; short- and long-horizon survey forecasts
predictor_family: Survey beliefs, heterogeneity, forward discounts, risk premia, and order flow
model_family: Narrative evidence synthesis
sample_design: Peer-reviewed synthesis of expectation surveys, forward-premium tests, microstructure studies, and forecast-performance evidence
benchmark: Rational expectations, constant risk premium, and homogeneous-belief models
pit_status: PARTIAL — Mixed—underlying surveys are timestamped, while the synthesis includes studies with varying real-time quality
native_result: The review concludes that both irrational expectations and time-varying risk premia contribute to the forward-discount anomaly and that long-horizon beliefs mean-revert.
costs_capacity: No unified cost-adjusted-return or capacity evaluation.
replication_decay: The synthesis documents persistent heterogeneity rather than one stable forecasting specification.
openness: Public repository metadata and author preprint are available; no machine-readable review extraction.
key_limitation: Narrative synthesis predates modern preregistered, multiple-testing, and real-time evaluation standards and cannot yield one pooled effect.

authors: Pasquale Della Corte; Lucio Sarno; Ilias Tsiakas
title: An Economic Evaluation of Empirical Exchange Rate Models
asset_class: FX—spot forecasts and carry-inclusive foreign-bond allocation
target: One-month spot exchange-rate return; decision value comes from a portfolio of domestic and foreign one-month bonds and is therefore carry-inclusive
predictor_family: Forward premium, monetary fundamentals, and volatility timing
model_family: Bayesian MCMC, stochastic volatility, model selection, and Bayesian forecast combinations
sample_design: Monthly 1971-2005 data with recursive out-of-sample forecasts and dynamic portfolio evaluation
benchmark: Random-walk-based dynamic strategy and individual empirical FX models
pit_status: PARTIAL — market prices and rates are dated, but a complete macro vintage reconstruction is absent
native_result: Forward-premium/stochastic-volatility and combined forecasts delivered large out-of-sample utility gains over the random-walk strategy.
costs_capacity: Break-even transaction costs were explicitly computed and the preferred strategies survived reasonably high modeled costs; impact and institutional capacity were not tested.
replication_decay: Subsequent economic-value studies are mixed; there is no sealed prospective or audited live replication of the exact strategy.
openness: Public author manuscript and repository metadata are available; no verified full code/data package.
key_limitation: Only three major currencies are studied, and model/portfolio choices were evaluated retrospectively on a common historical sample.

authors: Dennis Olson
title: Have Trading Rule Profits in the Currency Markets Declined over Time?
target: Moving-average trading-rule return on spot currencies; interest-rate carry treatment is incomplete
horizon: H1-H4; daily signals evaluated over five-year trading windows
predictor_family: Moving-average trend/technical rules
model_family: Rule optimization followed by successive chronological out-of-sample tests
sample_design: Daily 1971-2000 data; rules selected in five-year in-sample windows and tested in the next five-year windows
benchmark: Buy-and-hold/no-rule return and zero abnormal trading profit
pit_status: PIT — for spot signals; incomplete for a fully carry-inclusive investor return
native_result: Risk-adjusted rule profits fell from about 3.5% in the 1970s to approximately zero in the 1990s.
costs_capacity: Trading frictions and especially interest differentials are not treated comprehensively; no impact or capacity analysis.
replication_decay: Hutchinson et al. (2022) independently extended the decay through 2020 and found no cost-adjusted out-of-sample return after modest modeled costs.
openness: Stable publisher/RePEc metadata are public; no verified code/data package.
key_limitation: Normality assumptions, a restricted rule family, and incomplete carry accounting prevent a precise after-cost investor upper bound.

authors: Tobias J. Moskowitz; Yao Hua Ooi; Lasse Heje Pedersen
title: Time Series Momentum
target: Next-month excess returns
horizon: H3-H4; 1- to 12-month trend signal, monthly holding
predictor_family: Momentum and trend
model_family: Sign-of-past-return rules and predictive regressions
sample_design: Liquid futures and predecessor indices, January 1965-December 2009; 58 instruments across four asset classes
benchmark: Passive exposure, cross-sectional momentum, and standard risk factors
pit_status: PARTIAL — Signals use lagged returns; pre-futures index backfills and volatility scaling are retrospective
native_result: Returns persist for 1-12 months in every asset class, including bonds, then partially reverse at longer horizons
costs_capacity: Focuses on liquid futures and basic cost checks; roll slippage, margin, impact, and crowding are incomplete
replication_decay: Long-history trend studies are broadly supportive, but strategy definitions and post-publication decay vary
openness: Open-access article and author PDFs; full futures history proprietary
key_limitation: Cross-asset pooled significance and stitched histories are not a sealed bond-only test

authors: Mirko Marconi
title: Time Series Foundation Models for Multivariate Financial Time Series Forecasting
asset_class: Government bonds, foreign exchange, and equities
geography_market: U.S. Treasury yields, EUR/USD, and equity-market spread tasks
target: Yield-curve changes, FX volatility, and equity spread forecasts
predictor_family: Multivariate lagged financial time series
model_family: TimesFM-style Tiny Time Mixers and Chronos foundation models in zero-shot, fine-tuned, and from-scratch modes
sample_design: Three financial tasks with chronological tests and controlled comparisons as task-specific training history is reduced
benchmark: Naive persistence, econometric and specialized deep models, and from-scratch versions of the same architectures
pit_status: PARTIAL — Market tests are chronological, but foundation-model pretraining corpora and overlap with evaluation histories are not fully auditable
native_result: Zero-shot foundation models are competitive when little task-specific data are available, while specialized or trained-from-scratch models catch up or win as more local history is supplied
costs_capacity: Forecast losses are evaluated without portfolio construction, trading costs, market impact, or capacity
replication_decay: The three tasks expose heterogeneous transfer performance; the single-author preprint has no independent replication
openness: Preprint is public and uses accessible model families; complete experiment code and pretraining provenance were not verified
key_limitation: Only three tasks are studied and opaque pretraining overlap complicates a clean zero-shot claim

authors: Eugene F. Fama; Robert R. Bliss
title: The Information in Long-Maturity Forward Rates
target: One-year excess returns and subsequent spot-rate changes
horizon: H4-H5; one-year returns and multi-year rate changes
predictor_family: Carry, forward spreads, and curve
model_family: Predictive regressions
sample_design: Monthly U.S. Treasury zero-coupon data, 1964-1985; overlapping maturity-specific regressions
benchmark: Constant-premium expectations hypothesis
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Forward rates are dated at formation; coefficients and specifications use the full sample
native_result: Forward-spot spreads forecast annual excess returns; longer forwards also forecast later spot-rate changes through mean reversion
costs_capacity: No portfolio costs, financing, impact, or capacity analysis
replication_decay: Foundational lineage; later forward-rate OOS studies find mixed accuracy and often no economic value
openness: Public bibliographic record; article access and CRSP inputs may be licensed
key_limitation: In-sample overlapping regressions with no locked holdout or implementable decision test

authors: John Y. Campbell; Robert J. Shiller
title: Yield Spreads and Interest Rate Movements: A Bird's Eye View
target: Long-yield changes and future short-rate paths
horizon: H3-H6; maturity pairs from one month to ten years
predictor_family: Yield spreads and curve
model_family: Expectations-hypothesis regressions
sample_design: Postwar monthly McCulloch zero-coupon yields across many maturity pairs
benchmark: Expectations-theory coefficient and sign restrictions
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Yield spreads are observable at origin; inference and specification are full-sample
native_result: High spreads roughly forecast rising short rates but forecast falling long yields, opposite the constant-premium expectations theory
costs_capacity: No trading strategy or implementation frictions
replication_decay: The expectations-hypothesis rejection is durable; its translation into OOS return value is mixed
openness: DOI metadata and public working-paper copy available
key_limitation: Joint-hypothesis test cannot separate time-varying premia from expectation errors

authors: Gregory R. Duffee
title: Term Premia and Interest Rate Forecasts in Affine Models
target: Treasury yields at 6-month, 2-year, and 10-year maturities
predictor_family: Curve and latent term-premium state
model_family: Affine term-structure models
sample_design: Monthly 1952-1994 estimation; January 1995-December 1998 chronological holdout
benchmark: Random walk and completely affine models
pit_status: PIT — Pre-1995 estimation is separated from the holdout; yields are available at forecast origin
native_result: Standard affine models lose to the random walk; more flexible essentially affine models materially improve forecasts
costs_capacity: Forecast-accuracy study without a cost-adjusted trading mapping
replication_decay: Later DNS, FAVAR, and AFNS studies confirm strong model and horizon dependence
openness: Publisher DOI plus author and Federal Reserve PDFs; underlying yields partly licensed
key_limitation: Only four holdout years and no correction for trying multiple affine specifications

authors: John H. Cochrane; Monika Piazzesi
title: Bond Risk Premia
target: One-year excess returns on 2- to 5-year zero-coupon bonds
predictor_family: Forward-rate curve
model_family: Predictive regressions with a common return factor
sample_design: Monthly CRSP Fama-Bliss data, 1964-2003; overlapping annual returns
benchmark: Constant expected returns and conventional yield-curve factors
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Forward rates are observable, but the tent coefficients are selected and estimated on the full sample
native_result: One tent-shaped forward-rate factor explains up to 44% of annual excess-return variation across maturities
costs_capacity: No realistic portfolio costs, leverage limits, or capacity test
replication_decay: Thornton-Valente find no OOS utility; Bauer-Hamilton weaken inference; later Bayesian and ML studies recover gains
openness: AEA metadata, NBER and author PDFs public; CRSP data licensed
key_limitation: Large in-sample fit with overlapping returns and estimated factor weights

authors: Francis X. Diebold; Canlin Li
title: Forecasting the Term Structure of Government Bond Yields
target: The zero-coupon yield curve from 3 months to 10 years
predictor_family: Level, slope, and curvature
model_family: Dynamic Nelson-Siegel with AR/VAR factor dynamics
sample_design: Monthly 1985-2000 data; recursive forecasts from January 1994 through December 2000
benchmark: Random walk, slope regression, AR/VAR, and error-correction models
pit_status: PIT — Expanding estimation uses only prior yields at each retrospective forecast origin
native_result: One-year forecasts beat all standard competitors across reported maturities; one-month forecasts do not
costs_capacity: Yield loss only; no portfolio, turnover, or impact assessment
replication_decay: Many extensions reproduce longer-horizon gains, while random walks remain difficult at short horizons
openness: Publisher and NBER versions public; CRSP source data licensed
key_limitation: One historical regime and substantial performance heterogeneity by horizon

authors: Emanuel Moench
title: Forecasting the Yield Curve in a Data-Rich Environment: A No-Arbitrage Factor-Augmented VAR Approach
target: Treasury yields across the curve
predictor_family: Macroeconomic factors and short rate
model_family: No-arbitrage factor-augmented VAR
sample_design: Monthly 1983-2003 data; recursive OOS evaluation January 1994-September 2003
benchmark: Random walk, affine models, macro VAR, and dynamic Nelson-Siegel
pit_status: PARTIAL — Recursive fitting is chronological, but the large macro panel is not fully vintage-real-time
native_result: FAVAR significantly improves 6- and 12-month forecasts for most maturities; gains weaken at one month and very long maturities
costs_capacity: No decision-value or execution-cost test
replication_decay: Later macro-yield forecasting results remain specification- and vintage-sensitive
openness: DOI metadata and ECB working paper public; some source series licensed
key_limitation: Revised macro data can overstate information available at historical origins

authors: Sydney C. Ludvigson; Serena Ng
title: Macro Factors in Bond Risk Premia
target: One-year excess returns on 2- to 5-year bonds
predictor_family: Large-panel macroeconomic factors
model_family: Dynamic factors and predictive regressions
sample_design: 1964-2003, 132 monthly macro series; recursive OOS windows beginning 1985 and 1995
benchmark: Constant expected returns, forward spreads, and Cochrane-Piazzesi factor
pit_status: PARTIAL — Factors are recursively selected, but the macro panel uses revised rather than vintage releases
native_result: OOS forecast-error variance is roughly 84%-93% of the constant-return benchmark, depending on maturity and window
costs_capacity: No cost-adjusted portfolio or market-impact evaluation
replication_decay: Bauer-Hamilton weaken unspanned-factor inference; Gargano and corrected ML evidence remain supportive
openness: Author replication files and public paper; CRSP and some macro sources licensed
key_limitation: Historical revisions and predictor search weaken the real-time interpretation

authors: Jens H. E. Christensen; Francis X. Diebold; Glenn D. Rudebusch
title: The Affine Arbitrage-Free Class of Nelson-Siegel Term Structure Models
target: Treasury yields from 3 months to 30 years
predictor_family: Level, slope, curvature, and no-arbitrage restrictions
model_family: State-space arbitrage-free Nelson-Siegel
sample_design: Monthly 1987-2002 yields; expanding forecasts after a 1987-1996 initial window
benchmark: DNS variants, canonical affine model, and random walk
pit_status: PIT — Yield-only recursive forecasts; hyperparameters fixed by model specification
native_result: Parsimonious independent-factor AFNS is best in 14 of 18 horizon-maturity comparisons and beats flexible variants
costs_capacity: Forecast RMSE only; no trading implementation
replication_decay: Supports parsimony and no-arbitrage, but later model rankings vary across samples and rate regimes
openness: Journal DOI, NBER paper, and Federal Reserve PDF public
key_limitation: Small number of OOS observations, especially at 12 months

authors: Daniel L. Thornton; Giorgio Valente
title: Out-of-Sample Predictions of Bond Excess Returns and Forward Rates: An Asset-Allocation Perspective
target: One-year bond excess returns and portfolio utility
predictor_family: Forward spreads and forward-rate factor
model_family: Recursive and rolling regressions with mean-variance allocation
sample_design: Long monthly U.S. sample; OOS January 1970-December 2010 across 24 allocation specifications
benchmark: No-predictability expectations-hypothesis portfolio
pit_status: PIT — Forecast parameters and volatilities use only observations available before each origin
native_result: Forward-rate models deliver no systematic utility or Sharpe gain; performance deteriorates and is worst in the 2000s
costs_capacity: Small positive fees do not offset realistic transaction costs; impact and capacity remain unmodeled
replication_decay: Sarno-Schneider-Wagner align; Gargano and corrected neural-network studies find gains under richer models
openness: DOI, Federal Reserve working paper, and repository copy public
key_limitation: Mean-variance utility and covariance assumptions may miss nonlinear state dependence

authors: Don H. Kim; Athanasios Orphanides
title: Term Structure Estimation with Survey Data on Interest Rate Forecasts
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis
geography_market: United States Treasuries and professional rate surveys
target: Expected short-rate path, term premia, and longer-yield changes
horizon: H3-H5; short- and long-horizon survey paths
predictor_family: Professional surveys and yield curve
model_family: Three-factor affine-Gaussian term structure with survey moments
sample_design: U.S. Treasury yields and survey forecasts, 1990-2003
benchmark: Yield-only affine estimation and raw survey paths
pit_status: NOT-PIT — Survey observations are dated, but model parameters and evaluation use the full sample
native_result: Survey information stabilizes expected short rates and captures some short-run variation in surveyed longer-rate changes
costs_capacity: Term-premium estimation only; no trading or decision-value test
replication_decay: Subsequent survey-based decompositions support identification value, not necessarily return profitability
openness: Cambridge DOI and Federal Reserve working paper public
key_limitation: Average survey beliefs need not equal marginal-investor expectations; no heldout forecast comparison

authors: Anna Cieslak; Pavol Povala
title: Expected Returns in Treasury Bonds
target: One-year excess returns on 2- to 20-year bonds
predictor_family: Inflation expectations and maturity-specific yield cycles
model_family: Yield decomposition and predictive regressions
sample_design: Monthly CMT yields, November 1971-December 2011; recursive OOS windows starting 1978, 1985, and 1995
benchmark: Forward rates, forward-spot spreads, yield PCs, and historical mean
pit_status: PIT — Lagged yields and inflation history; survey robustness preserves original survey frequency
native_result: The cycle factor forecasts returns in and out of sample and subsumes the Cochrane-Piazzesi forward-rate factor
costs_capacity: No cost-adjusted trading, financing, or capacity analysis
replication_decay: Bauer-Hamilton cautions on spanning inference; corrected ML also finds nonlinear macro-curve information
openness: DOI and author PDF public; source yield and survey data documented
key_limitation: Trend-inflation calibration and repeated OOS start dates add researcher discretion

authors: Lucio Sarno; Paul Schneider; Christian Wagner
title: The Economic Value of Predicting Bond Risk Premia
target: Bond excess returns and investor utility
horizon: H3-H4; 25 horizon-maturity pairs from one month to ten years
predictor_family: Curve, term premia, and macro uncertainty
model_family: Affine term-structure estimation and portfolio choice
sample_design: Monthly U.S. rates, 1952-2012; recursive OOS estimation after an initial ten-year window
benchmark: Expectations-hypothesis constant-risk-premium forecasts
pit_status: PARTIAL — Recursive yield-based fitting is chronological; spliced historical curve construction remains ex post
native_result: High statistical forecast fit does not beat EH portfolios economically; value is positive mainly in high-uncertainty states
costs_capacity: Utility comparison omits full spread, impact, financing, and leverage frictions
replication_decay: Confirms Thornton-Valente's economic null; Gargano obtains gains with volatility dynamics and model averaging
openness: DOI metadata and open institutional manuscript
key_limitation: Economic conclusions depend on utility, covariance, and portfolio-constraint choices

authors: Ralph S. J. Koijen; Tobias J. Moskowitz; Lasse Heje Pedersen; Evert B. Vrugt
title: Carry
geography_market: Ten developed sovereign bond markets and U.S. Treasury maturity portfolios
target: Next-period government-bond and curve-position returns
predictor_family: Carry, roll, and curve slope
model_family: Cross-sectional and time-series portfolio sorts
sample_design: Global bonds as early as November 1983-September 2012; U.S. Treasuries August 1971-September 2012
benchmark: Value, cross-sectional momentum, time-series momentum, and global factors
pit_status: PARTIAL — Carry is ex ante from current curves; synthetic-futures construction and data stitching are retrospective
native_result: Carry predicts returns across and within asset classes, including bonds, with alpha to value and momentum factors
costs_capacity: Uses estimated transaction costs; nonlinear impact, financing stress, and capacity are not audited
replication_decay: Broad carry evidence spans markets, but no frozen prospective government-bond implementation is public
openness: DOI, NBER, and accepted manuscript public; several market inputs proprietary
key_limitation: Cross-asset design and synthetic histories obscure bond-only independent evidence

authors: Michael D. Bauer; James D. Hamilton
title: Robust Bond Risk Premia
target: One-year bond excess-return predictability beyond yield-curve PCs
predictor_family: Macro, supply, inflation, and curve factors
model_family: Parametric-bootstrap spanning tests
sample_design: Independent reanalysis of six prominent studies under small-sample-corrected null simulations
benchmark: Spanning by level, slope, and curvature
pit_status: NOT-APPLICABLE — Methodological reanalysis; not a deployable forecast record
native_result: Conventional tests are severely oversized; robust evidence against yield-curve spanning is much weaker than reported
costs_capacity: No strategy or cost analysis; the result concerns statistical evidence
replication_decay: Directly downgrades several unspanned-predictor lineages; later Bayesian and ML findings remain contested
openness: DOI, NBER, Federal Reserve, and author PDFs public
key_limitation: Bootstrap validity depends on the fitted null dynamics and focuses on spanning, not all forecast value

authors: Antonio Gargano; Davide Pettenuzzo; Allan Timmermann
title: Bond Return Predictability: Economic Value and Links to the Macroeconomy
target: One-year bond excess returns and certainty-equivalent utility
predictor_family: Forward spreads, forward-rate factor, macro factor, and surveys
model_family: Bayesian predictive regressions and forecast combinations
sample_design: Recursive real-time-style OOS evaluation, 1990-2015, for 2- to 5-year bonds
benchmark: Expectations hypothesis and simpler OLS predictor models
pit_status: PARTIAL — Lagged predictors and recursive estimation; macro release vintages are not fully audited
native_result: Several models have significantly positive OOS R-squared; volatility dynamics and combinations produce sizable utility gains
costs_capacity: Accounts for estimation and model uncertainty, but not comprehensive trading costs or impact
replication_decay: Reconciles earlier nulls through richer dynamics; independent fresh-era and live validation remain absent
openness: DOI metadata and public author manuscript; some underlying data licensed
key_limitation: Model search and revised macro data can make the exercise less real-time than claimed

authors: Daniele Bianchi; Matthias Buchner; Tobias Hoogteijling; Andrea Tamoni
title: Bond Risk Premiums with Machine Learning; Corrigendum
target: One-year excess returns on 2- to 10-year bonds
predictor_family: Yield-curve and high-dimensional macro features
model_family: Trees, penalized regressions, and neural networks
sample_design: Monthly 1971-2018; recursive train-validation-test forecasts beginning January 1989; corrected information set
benchmark: Historical mean, PCA regressions, and penalized linear models
pit_status: PIT — Corrigendum removes information unavailable at forecast time; original results were contaminated
native_result: Corrected OOS R-squared values decline, but neural-network predictability remains statistically and economically significant
costs_capacity: Portfolio utility is modeled; execution costs, leverage, and capacity are incomplete
replication_decay: Formal corrigendum materially reduces effect size; independent fresh-era replication is still lacking
openness: Original DOI and public corrigendum; data inputs are partly licensed
key_limitation: Post-correction evidence remains based on one repeatedly studied historical test era

authors: Edward Nelling; Joseph Gyourko
title: The Predictability of Equity REIT Returns
target: Monthly REIT returns and strategy payoffs
predictor_family: Momentum, reversal, trend, seasonality, and technical rules
model_family: Autoregressive tests and nonparametric persistence analysis
sample_design: Monthly equity REIT returns from 1975-1995, compared with small- and mid-cap stocks and split across subperiods.
benchmark: Zero autocorrelation, small- and mid-cap stocks, and typical transaction costs
pit_status: PIT — for lagged returns; no locked model-selection holdout
native_result: Monthly returns are statistically predictable, but the magnitude does not cover typical transaction costs and individual-REIT persistence is limited.
costs_capacity: Typical transaction costs eliminate the reported opportunity; detailed market-impact and capacity estimates are absent.
replication_decay: Ling, Naranjo, and Ryngaert (2000) independently find weak 1990s OOS performance and disappearing cost-adjusted profits under modeled costs.
openness: Verified DOI and public abstract; no code or data archive.
key_limitation: Retrospective tests precede the modern REIT market and do not use a sealed OOS design.

authors: David C. Ling; Andy Naranjo; Michael D. Ryngaert
title: The Predictability of Equity REIT Returns: Time Variation and Economic Significance
venue: The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics
target: One-month excess REIT returns and active-strategy returns
predictor_family: Valuation and macroeconomic variables
model_family: Rolling predictive regressions with best-subset model selection
sample_design: Monthly data from 1980-1996; every predictor subset is fit in a rolling 60-month window and the best adjusted-R-squared model forecasts the next month.
benchmark: REIT buy-and-hold and excess returns over T-bills, the S&P 500, and small-cap stocks
pit_status: PARTIAL — rolling lagged predictors are used, but macro-data vintages and repeated subset search are not sealed
native_result: OOS predictability is far below in-sample fit, is effectively absent in the 1990s, and modest gross active returns largely disappear after transaction costs.
costs_capacity: Transaction costs are included and remove most gains; impact and capacity are not separately modeled.
replication_decay: Supports Nelling and Gyourko's after-cost null; later regime and dynamic-model studies find only model- and horizon-specific pockets of value.
openness: Public working-paper PDF and verified DOI; no code or machine-readable data archive.
key_limitation: Selecting the best of all predictor subsets every month creates substantial search risk without nested model-selection correction.

authors: Omokolade Akinsomi; Goodness C. Aye; Vassilios Babalos; Fotini Economou; Rangan Gupta
title: Real Estate Returns Predictability Revisited: Novel Evidence from the US REITs Market
target: REIT returns and allocation performance
predictor_family: Macroeconomic, monetary-policy, sentiment, and uncertainty variables
model_family: Dynamic model averaging and selection, TVP, BMA, and recursive AR
sample_design: Monthly U.S. REIT data from 1991-01 to 2014-12; recursive forecasts compare six model classes under parameter instability.
benchmark: Recursive AR(4) and buy-and-hold
pit_status: PARTIAL — recursive estimation is chronological, but vintage macro and sentiment inputs are not fully reconstructed
native_result: Dynamic model selection performs best overall; useful predictors vary through time and strategies based on forecasts outperform buy-and-hold in the reported exercise.
costs_capacity: No complete spread, turnover, tax, impact, or capacity stress test.
replication_decay: Guidolin, Pedio, and Petrova (2023) also find OOS pockets of REIT return value, while earlier rolling studies report weak cost-adjusted results under modeled costs.
openness: Public institutional manuscript and verified DOI; no complete code or data-vintage archive.
key_limitation: No sealed final holdout, many predictors and models, and unclear real-time availability for revised macro and sentiment series.

authors: Matteo Bonato; Oğuzhan Çepni; Rangan Gupta; Christian Pierdzioch
title: Forecasting Realized Volatility of International REITs: The Role of Realized Skewness and Realized Kurtosis
geography_market: Nine leading international REIT markets and regions
target: Realized, good, and bad REIT volatility
predictor_family: Realized volatility, jumps, skewness, and kurtosis
model_family: HAR realized-volatility regressions
sample_design: Five-minute REIT-index data from 2008-09 to 2020-08; expanding-window OOS forecasts with about 1,000 initial observations and roughly 2,000 forecasts.
benchmark: HAR-RV and HAR-RV-jump models
pit_status: PIT — for lagged intraday measures; vendor corrections and synchronized market-hour revisions are not archived
native_result: Realized skewness and kurtosis significantly improve daily, weekly, and monthly OOS volatility forecasts beyond realized jumps, including good and bad volatility.
costs_capacity: Risk-forecast study; no trading or hedging execution-cost analysis.
replication_decay: Related international REIT volatility studies find gains from oil uncertainty and global conditions, but many share authors and overlapping data.
openness: Public institutional manuscript and verified DOI; intraday data and code are not fully open.
key_limitation: Overlapping horizons and multiple markets and targets raise multiplicity concerns; no prospective risk-management decision test.

authors: Afees A. Salisu; Rangan Gupta; Elie Bouri
title: Testing the Forecasting Power of Global Economic Conditions for the Volatility of International REITs Using a GARCH-MIDAS Approach
venue: The Quarterly Review of Economics and Finance
geography_market: International REIT indices, including United States and emerging markets
target: Daily REIT return volatility
predictor_family: Global macroeconomic conditions
model_family: GARCH-MIDAS and principal-component forecast combinations
sample_design: Daily international REIT returns and monthly global-condition indices from 1990-01 to 2021-06, with in-sample and OOS comparisons.
benchmark: GARCH-MIDAS realized-volatility model without global economic conditions
pit_status: PARTIAL — mixed-frequency lags are used, but release vintages for global-condition indices are not reconstructed
native_result: Adding global economic conditions yields forecast gains, especially for U.S. and emerging-market REIT volatility; alternative global indices are weaker unless combined.
costs_capacity: A higher-return application is discussed, but turnover, spreads, impact, and capacity are not fully reported.
replication_decay: Related positive papers use overlapping authors and similar international REIT samples, limiting independence.
openness: Public institutional record and working-paper metadata; verified DOI; no full code or vintage-data archive.
key_limitation: Revised global indices, many regions and variants, and overlapping-author follow-ups weaken real-time and independent-validation claims.

authors: Massimo Guidolin; Manuela Pedio; Milena T. Petrova
title: The Predictability of Real Estate Excess Returns: An Out-of-Sample Economic Value Analysis
venue: The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics
asset_class: Listed REITs and private real estate boundary
geography_market: United States NAREIT and NCREIF indices
target: Excess public and private real-estate returns and portfolio utility
horizon: H3-H4: short and intermediate horizons, including six months
predictor_family: Valuation, macroeconomic, and cross-asset variables
model_family: Recursive linear and Markov-switching predictive models
sample_design: Recursive OOS forecasts for equity NAREIT and appraisal-based NCREIF excess returns, followed by mean-variance allocation among stocks, bonds, cash, and real estate.
benchmark: Historical sample mean, linear models, and no-real-estate-timing portfolios
pit_status: PARTIAL — recursive forecasts are chronological, but appraisal revisions and macro-data vintages are not fully versioned
native_result: Markov-switching models deliver pockets of OOS accuracy and utility, strongest for smoothed private real estate and at intermediate horizons; gains extend to public REITs and survive the modeled transaction costs.
costs_capacity: Transaction costs are included, but leverage, impact, allocation delay, private-fund gates, and capacity are not fully modeled.
replication_decay: No sealed or prospective replication; the stronger private-market result is mechanically aided by appraisal persistence and is not comparable with executable REIT returns.
openness: Public working-paper version and verified DOI; no complete code, vintage-data, or appraisal-revision archive.
key_limitation: Public and appraisal-based private returns have different observability and executability, and regime selection is evaluated on one historical record.

authors: Francis X. Diebold; Roberto S. Mariano
title: Comparing Predictive Accuracy
target: Equal expected forecast loss
predictor_family: Any forecast information set
model_family: Diebold-Mariano loss-differential test
sample_design: Asymptotic comparison of paired forecast-loss differentials with serial-correlation-robust variance estimation and finite-sample illustrations.
benchmark: Null of equal predictive accuracy under the same target, dates, horizon, and loss
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable—method evaluates already-issued forecast sequences
native_result: Provides a generally applicable test of equal predictive accuracy that accommodates non-Gaussian, serially correlated, and contemporaneously correlated forecast errors.
costs_capacity: Not addressed; the loss must itself encode any implementation costs relevant to the decision.
replication_decay: Foundational pairwise framework; later records refine parameter uncertainty, nesting, conditioning, multiple models, and multiple horizons.
openness: Publisher record and fully specified statistic support independent reimplementation.
key_limitation: The usual normal approximation can be poorly sized in small samples, with nested models, or when the long-run variance is weakly estimated.

authors: Kenneth D. West
title: Asymptotic Inference about Predictive Ability
target: Moments of out-of-sample predictions and prediction errors
predictor_family: Any estimated forecasting model
model_family: West predictive-ability inference
sample_design: Long-sequence asymptotics and simulations for smooth functions of forecasts when model parameters are estimated rather than known.
benchmark: Naive forecast-error inference that treats estimated parameters as fixed
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable—method conditions on a defined recursive or rolling forecast experiment
native_result: Derives variance corrections for parameter-estimation effects and shows in simulation that the procedures can work at empirically relevant sample sizes.
costs_capacity: Not addressed; applicable to cost-aware losses if prespecified.
replication_decay: Extended by nested-model and conditional-predictive-ability procedures in METH-0003 through METH-0005.
openness: Publisher record and complete asymptotic derivations support reimplementation.
key_limitation: Validity depends on the estimator, sample split, smoothness, and asymptotic regime matching the forecast exercise.

authors: Dean Croushore; Tom Stark
title: A Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists
target: Forecasts and empirical results using information actually available at each date
predictor_family: Macroeconomic variables and data vintages
model_family: Real-time vintage database
sample_design: Quarterly snapshots beginning in November 1965 reconstruct the historical data releases available to forecasters and demonstrate forecast sensitivity to revisions.
benchmark: Latest-revised macroeconomic series substituted for the historical information set
pit_status: PIT—vintage snapshots explicitly reconstruct origin-available releases
native_result: Data revisions can materially alter forecasts; a vintage panel provides the infrastructure needed for valid real-time pseudo-out-of-sample evaluation.
costs_capacity: Not applicable.
replication_decay: The public vintage system supports the forecasting and robustness studies in METH-0023 and METH-0024.
openness: The Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists is publicly maintained by the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.
key_limitation: Vintage coverage is strongest for major U.S. macro series and does not reconstruct every private, market, or intraday release.

authors: Tom Stark; Dean Croushore
title: Forecasting with a Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists
target: Real output growth forecasts
predictor_family: Real-time output vintages
model_family: ARIMA and repeated-observation forecasting
sample_design: Re-estimates quarterly output-growth forecasts across 136 historical vintages from November 1965 through August 1999 and compares alternative definitions of realized outcomes.
benchmark: Forecast evaluation using one latest-revised data series
pit_status: PIT—each forecast uses the corresponding historical vintage
native_result: Forecasts, model selection, and measured accuracy can vary with the input vintage and with the chosen definition of the eventual actual.
costs_capacity: Not applicable.
replication_decay: Empirical use of the infrastructure in METH-0022; confirms that vintage choice is not merely a metadata issue.
openness: Public real-time data and published design permit replication.
key_limitation: The application is centered on U.S. aggregate output and univariate models, so magnitudes do not transfer automatically to market predictors.

authors: Dean Croushore; Tom Stark
title: A Real-Time Data Set for Macroeconomists: Does the Data Vintage Matter?
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics
target: Robustness of published macroeconomic results to data vintage
predictor_family: Macroeconomic vintage data
model_family: Cross-vintage replication
sample_design: Recomputes prominent empirical macroeconomic exercises across quarterly vintage snapshots and studies revision properties.
benchmark: Original published result or latest-vintage replication
pit_status: PIT—historical releases are explicitly versioned
native_result: Some empirical conclusions are robust across vintages while others change materially, establishing data vintage as a design variable rather than a clerical choice.
costs_capacity: Not applicable.
replication_decay: Externally validates the importance of the dataset in METH-0022 across several published applications.
openness: Public vintage database; article documents the replicated exercises.
key_limitation: The selected macroeconomic studies are illustrative rather than a census of financial-predictability results.

authors: Raffaella Giacomini; Halbert White
title: Tests of Conditional Predictive Ability
target: Conditional expected loss differentials
predictor_family: State-dependent forecast performance
model_family: Conditional predictive-ability test
sample_design: Fixed-window asymptotics evaluate forecasting methods rather than population models and compare macro forecasts using conditioning instruments.
benchmark: Unconditional equal-accuracy tests and unconditional model ranking
pit_status: PIT — compatible when conditioning variables are available at each forecast origin
native_result: Conditional tests can detect state-dependent performance hidden by unconditional averages and accommodate nested or nonnested methods under heterogeneous data.
costs_capacity: Decision-relevant costs can enter the loss but are not analyzed in the application.
replication_decay: Complements rather than supersedes unconditional tests; inference targets the chosen estimation window and conditioning set.
openness: Publisher article and public manuscript disclose the test and empirical design.
key_limitation: Results are conditional on user-chosen instruments and a fixed estimation-window asymptotic framework.

authors: Tilmann Gneiting; Adrian E. Raftery
title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
target: Probabilistic forecast distributions
predictor_family: Any probabilistic information set
model_family: Strictly proper scoring rules
sample_design: General theory and review of proper scores on probability spaces, including logarithmic, quadratic, continuous ranked probability, and energy scores, with a forecast case study.
benchmark: Improper or ad hoc scores that reward strategically distorted probabilities
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable—score validity is a decision-theoretic property
native_result: Strict propriety makes truthful predictive distributions uniquely optimal in expectation and supplies coherent tools for calibration, sharpness, comparison, and estimation.
costs_capacity: Not addressed; scores evaluate distributions rather than executable portfolios.
replication_decay: Foundational synthesis; later work specializes consistent scores to point forecasts, latent volatility, and joint risk measures.
openness: Public author manuscript and publisher DOI expose the full theory.
key_limitation: A proper score does not choose the user's economic loss, solve dependence-aware inference, or guarantee adequate tail power.

authors: Tilmann Gneiting
title: Making and Evaluating Point Forecasts
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
target: Means, quantiles, expectiles, and other point functionals
predictor_family: Any point-forecast information set
model_family: Consistent scoring functions and elicitability
sample_design: Characterization theorems and examples linking a forecast directive to the class of scoring functions consistent for that functional.
benchmark: Routine use of squared or absolute error without matching the intended target functional
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable—methodological target-score alignment
native_result: Shows that mismatched scoring functions can reverse forecast rankings; means require Bregman scores and quantiles require generalized piecewise-linear scores.
costs_capacity: Not addressed.
replication_decay: Extends the proper-score logic of METH-0008 to point forecasts and motivates joint elicitability work in METH-0011.
openness: Public manuscript and publisher article provide proofs and examples.
key_limitation: Elicitability and statistical consistency do not by themselves determine the economically relevant decision functional.

authors: David H. Bailey; Marcos López de Prado
title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting, and Non-Normality
target: Statistical significance of a selected strategy's Sharpe ratio
predictor_family: Searched trading strategies
model_family: Deflated Sharpe Ratio
sample_design: Analytical and numerical adjustment of the selected Sharpe ratio for trial count, cross-trial variance, sample length, skewness, and kurtosis.
benchmark: Naive Sharpe ratio or probabilistic Sharpe ratio that ignores strategy selection
pit_status: NOT-APPLICABLE — Requires a logged, pre-evaluation count and dependence-adjusted estimate of tried configurations
native_result: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio lowers apparent significance when many configurations were searched or returns are non-normal, separating some statistical flukes from stronger findings.
costs_capacity: Applicable to net return series, but the statistic does not estimate missing transaction costs or market impact.
replication_decay: Complements the explicit overfitting-probability framework in METH-0019 and multiple-testing haircuts in METH-0020.
openness: Public author manuscript discloses formulas and examples.
key_limitation: Results are unreliable when the number and dependence of trials are hidden or reconstructed selectively.

authors: Campbell R. Harvey; Yan Liu
title: Backtesting
target: Multiple-testing-adjusted Sharpe ratio and required strategy return
predictor_family: Searched investment strategies
model_family: Haircut Sharpe ratio and profit hurdle
sample_design: Calibrates p-value, Sharpe-ratio, and return hurdles to the number and dependence of tests using simulation and empirical test-distribution inputs.
benchmark: Reported backtest Sharpe ratio under a single-test assumption
pit_status: NOT-APPLICABLE — Requires the strategy search count and sampling frequency; not itself a PIT validation
native_result: Multiple testing can require large nonlinear haircuts to reported Sharpe ratios and higher profit hurdles than conventional single-test inference.
costs_capacity: Profit hurdles can be applied after costs, but the article does not estimate strategy-specific impact or capacity.
replication_decay: Operationalizes the factor-zoo logic of METH-0016 for practitioners and overlaps conceptually with METH-0018.
openness: Authors provide public MATLAB code and calibration inputs for Haircut_SR and Profit_Hurdle.
key_limitation: The haircut is only as credible as the supplied number, dependence, and distribution of attempted tests.

authors: Tobias Fissler; Johanna F. Ziegel
title: Higher Order Elicitability and Osband's Principle
target: Joint risk-functionals including Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall
predictor_family: Distributional and tail-risk information
model_family: Jointly elicitable functionals and strictly consistent scores
sample_design: General mathematical characterization of multidimensional elicitability and scoring functions via Osband's principle.
benchmark: Standalone scoring of non-elicitable Expected Shortfall
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable—theoretical score construction
native_result: Although Expected Shortfall is not singly elicitable, the pair of Value at Risk and Expected Shortfall is jointly elicitable under mild conditions, enabling valid comparative backtests.
costs_capacity: Not addressed.
replication_decay: Supplies the theoretical basis for later joint VaR-ES forecast evaluation; no market-performance claim is made.
openness: Open Project Euclid article and supplementary material.
key_limitation: Joint elicitability requires evaluating the full vector with an appropriate score; it does not validate a misspecified dynamic risk model.

authors: Rob Arnott; Campbell R. Harvey; Harry Markowitz
title: A Backtesting Protocol in the Era of Machine Learning
venue: The Journal of Financial Data Science
target: Credibility of machine-learning and quantitative-finance backtests
predictor_family: High-dimensional features and strategy searches
model_family: Seven-point backtesting protocol
sample_design: Conceptual protocol covering research motivation, complete trial accounting, sample choice, data integrity, model construction, implementation, and disclosure.
benchmark: Unlogged iterative machine-learning backtests with a repeatedly consulted test set
pit_status: NOT-APPLICABLE — Protocol requires chronological validation and origin-available data but presents no prospective trial of the protocol
native_result: Codifies controls for false discovery in data-scarce, adaptive financial ML and emphasizes that model flexibility increases rather than removes classic backtesting risks.
costs_capacity: Explicitly requires implementation realism, but supplies no universal cost or capacity estimator.
replication_decay: Synthesizes earlier multiple-testing and overfitting results; the protocol's incremental effect on live performance is not independently measured.
openness: Public author manuscript includes the complete seven-point protocol.
key_limitation: A checklist depends on auditable compliance and cannot quantify undisclosed researcher degrees of freedom by itself.

authors: Alejandro Lopez-Lira; Yuehua Tang; Mingyin Zhu
title: The Memorization Problem: Can We Trust LLMs' Economic Forecasts?
geography_market: U.S. and international macroeconomic and financial series
target: Identification of genuine LLM forecasting skill inside and after training windows
predictor_family: Economic releases, market levels, securities, headlines, and embeddings
model_family: LLM memorization audit and non-identification framework
sample_design: Theory proves observational equivalence between skill and recall for pre-cutoff outcomes; empirical tests query exact market and macro values, constrained prompts, masking, entity reconstruction, embeddings, and post-cutoff controls.
benchmark: Post-knowledge-cutoff recall and prompt-based instructions to ignore future information
pit_status: PIT failure for pre-cutoff tasks; only outcomes strictly after an auditable frozen cutoff identify forecasting skill
native_result: LLMs recall exact pre-cutoff economic and financial values; prompt restrictions and masking do not remove encoded future information, while post-cutoff recall disappears. Pre-cutoff counterfactual forecasting skill is therefore non-identified.
costs_capacity: Not a trading-cost study; it invalidates the information set before economic evaluation.
replication_decay: Methodological correction to historical LLM backtests that overlap training data; METH-0032 applies stricter decision-time data controls but remains retrospective and underpowered.
openness: Open arXiv manuscript documents tests and results; proprietary model training corpora remain unavailable.
key_limitation: Preprint evidence relies heavily on closed models whose weights, exact corpora, and changing service checkpoints cannot be independently inspected.

authors: Mostapha Benhenda
title: Look-Ahead-Bench: a Standardized Benchmark of Look-ahead Bias in Point-in-Time LLMs for Finance
target: Alpha decay across LLM training-window and post-cutoff regimes
predictor_family: Agentic fundamental, valuation, sentiment, and technical inputs
model_family: Standard foundation models versus point-in-time LLMs
sample_design: Compares matched 2021 and 2024 market periods using Llama 3.1, DeepSeek 3.2, three proprietary PiT-Inference models, an open-source agent harness, and quantitative trading baselines.
benchmark: Buy-and-hold, equal weight, momentum, mean reversion, moving-average crossover, and random signals
pit_status: PARTIAL — standard-model cutoff dates are explicit, while proprietary PiT training and decontamination cannot be independently audited
native_result: Standard LLM agents lose 15.25 to 21.77 percentage points of alpha after their cutoffs, while the tested PiT models show alpha changes from 0.31 to 1.30 points and improve with scale.
costs_capacity: Portfolio returns are benchmark simulations without full realized trading costs, borrow, impact, financing, or deployment capacity.
replication_decay: Extends METH-0033 and METH-0034 with an alpha-decay benchmark; no independent replication or live execution exists by the cutoff.
openness: Open arXiv manuscript and public benchmark code repository; proprietary PiT model weights and training data are closed.
key_limitation: Single-author proof of concept uses two short market regimes, a limited universe, and vendor-supplied proprietary PiT models.

authors: Qianqian Xie; Weiguang Han; Zhengyu Chen; Ruoyu Xiang; Xiao Zhang; Yueru He; Mengxi Xiao; Dong Li; Yongfu Dai; Duanyu Feng; Yijing Xu; Haoqiang Kang; Ziyan Kuang; Chenhan Yuan; Kailai Yang; Zheheng Luo; Tianlin Zhang; Zhiwei Liu; Guojun Xiong; Zhiyang Deng; Yuechen Jiang; Zhiyuan Yao; Haohang Li; Yangyang Yu; Gang Hu; Jiajia Huang; Xiao-Yang Liu; Alejandro Lopez-Lira; Benyou Wang; Yanzhao Lai; Hao Wang; Min Peng; Sophia Ananiadou; Jimin Huang
title: FinBen: A Holistic Financial Benchmark for Large Language Models
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 37, Datasets and Benchmarks Track
asset_class: Mixed financial domains, including equities and trading tasks
geography_market: Primarily English-language and U.S.-oriented public financial datasets
target: Twenty-four financial NLP, reasoning, forecasting, and stock-trading tasks
horizon: Task dependent, from document classification to daily trading (H0-H4)
predictor_family: News, filings, financial text, questions, and market context
model_family: Twenty-one general and finance-specialized large language models
sample_design: Forty-two public datasets consolidated into a unified held-out benchmark with standardized prompts and evaluation
benchmark: Cross-model leaderboard spanning open, closed, general, and finance-specific LLMs
pit_status: PARTIAL — Dataset splits are held out, but undocumented pretraining overlap and memorization cannot be ruled out for many evaluated models
native_result: LLMs perform well on several information-extraction and sentiment tasks but remain weak and unstable on numerical reasoning, forecasting, and stock trading; no model dominates all tasks
costs_capacity: Trading tasks are benchmark simulations without realistic spreads, impact, borrow, latency, API cost, or capital capacity
replication_decay: A shared task produced independent submissions on the same benchmark, but not a new point-in-time market sample
openness: Datasets, benchmark code, and public leaderboard are released; some closed-model weights and training corpora remain opaque
key_limitation: Public test sets can enter pretraining or prompt-development loops, and benchmark accuracy is not a prospective investment record

authors: Tim Bollerslev; James Marrone; Lai Xu; Hao Zhou
title: Stock Return Predictability and Variance Risk Premia: Statistical Inference and International Evidence
venue: Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis 49(3): 633-661
asset_class: National equity indices and index options
geography_market: United States, France, Germany, Japan, Switzerland, Netherlands, Belgium, and United Kingdom
target: Aggregate country equity returns
horizon: H3-H4—monthly through annual, peaking around two to four months
predictor_family: Country and global variance risk premia
model_family: Country predictive regressions, panel regressions, and finite-sample Monte Carlo inference
sample_design: Country-specific liquid-option-market samples plus cross-country panel restrictions; simulation checks address overlapping-regression finite-sample bias.
benchmark: Country-specific VRP and conventional overlapping-return inference
pit_status: PIT—country and global VRP are formed from quotes and realized variation available at the forecast origin
native_result: Forecast accuracy: seven non-U.S. countries display similar horizon patterns, and a global VRP yields stronger, nearly identical cross-country predictability. Trading P&L: not evaluated.
costs_capacity: No country-ETF or futures implementation, currency hedge, transaction-cost, or capacity analysis.
replication_decay: Provides external-market corroboration of the U.S. VRP lineage, though not a prospective replication.
openness: Published article and public PDF are available; international option data are licensed.
key_limitation: The evidence reuses the same broad historical era and method family and remains retrospective.

authors: David Geltner
title: Smoothing in Appraisal-Based Returns
venue: The Journal of Real Estate Finance and Economics
target: Latent return volatility, covariance, and autocorrelation
horizon: H4-H5: quarterly to multi-year risk measurement
predictor_family: Lagged appraisals and stale valuations
model_family: Partial-adjustment appraisal-smoothing models and unsmoothing estimators
sample_design: Conceptual measurement study with limited empirical evidence from appraisal-based commercial real-estate return series.
benchmark: Observed appraisal returns versus latent market-value returns
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable: measurement and identification study
native_result: Appraisal smoothing mechanically lowers measured second moments and induces persistence; appraisal returns require unsmoothing before risk inference.
costs_capacity: Illiquidity and sparse transactions are the source of non-executability; no trading strategy is claimed.
replication_decay: A large later literature confirms smoothing, while Bond et al. (2012) and Couts et al. (2024) show simple aggregate unsmoothing can over- or under-correct.
openness: Verified DOI and public metadata; no code or source-data archive.
key_limitation: Latent market values are not observed, so unsmoothing depends on structural assumptions and cannot create executable returns.

authors: Spencer J. Couts; Andrei S. Gonçalves; Andrea Rossi
title: Unsmoothing Returns of Illiquid Funds
asset_class: Private commercial real estate and hedge funds
geography_market: United States private CRE funds and global hedge funds
target: Systematic risk, alpha, volatility, and spurious autocorrelation
predictor_family: Lagged reported returns and common stale-mark components
model_family: Generalized three-step AR and MA unsmoothing
sample_design: Hedge-fund returns from 1995-2017 and quarterly NCREIF open-end private real-estate fund returns from 29 funds over 1994-2017.
benchmark: Observed returns and traditional one-step Geltner or Getmansky-Lo-Makarov unsmoothing
pit_status: NOT-PIT — t applicable: risk-measurement correction
native_result: Common spurious autocorrelation survives traditional unsmoothing; the generalized method raises private-CRE public-market beta from 0.07 to 0.34 and lowers annual alpha from 4.3% observed to 1.6%.
costs_capacity: Measured fund returns are illiquid and not continuously executable; gates, appraisal lags, and fund-level fees remain outside a public trading strategy.
replication_decay: Extends and qualifies Geltner-style unsmoothing; no independent exact replication of the generalized estimator is available by the cutoff.
openness: Public manuscript and verified DOI; commercial hedge-fund and NCREIF data are restricted.
key_limitation: Economic returns remain latent and results depend on proxy public factors and a small 29-fund private-CRE panel.

authors: Steven N. Kaplan; Antoinette Schoar
title: Private Equity Performance: Returns, Persistence, and Capital Flows
geography_market: Venture Economics buyout and venture funds
target: Next-fund performance and public-market-equivalent returns
horizon: H6: successive fund vintages, generally more than five years
predictor_family: Prior fund performance and manager track record
model_family: PME measurement, persistence regressions, and performance sorts
sample_design: Main sample of 746 largely liquidated funds above $5 million in 1990 dollars, chiefly pre-1995 vintages, with a broader 1,090-fund Venture Economics sample covering 1980-2001.
benchmark: S&P 500 PME and prior-fund performance
pit_status: NOT-PIT — for the allocator claim: final prior-fund performance is generally unavailable when the next fund is raised
native_result: Net average returns approximately match the S&P 500, and final performance appears strongly persistent across successive funds of the same partnership.
costs_capacity: Net-of-fee fund cash flows are used, but illiquidity, commitment pacing, access, and secondary-market costs are not fully captured.
replication_decay: Later deal-level and Burgiss studies find buyout persistence declines and largely disappears post-2000 when only information available at fundraising is used; VC persistence survives better.
openness: Public author manuscript and verified DOI; Venture Economics data are proprietary.
key_limitation: The persistence signal uses ex post final performance, an old selected sample, and information unavailable at the actual allocation decision.

authors: Gregory W. Brown; Oleg R. Gredil; Steven N. Kaplan
title: Do Private Equity Funds Manipulate Reported Returns?
target: Interim NAV marks, later performance, and follow-on fundraising
predictor_family: Interim reported performance and fundraising incentives
model_family: Panel regressions and valuation-unwinding tests
sample_design: Burgiss quarterly cash flows and NAVs for 2,071 funds from more than 200 institutional investors, supplemented with StepStone firm data.
benchmark: Subsequent realized performance, valuation unwinding, and follow-on fundraising outcomes
pit_status: PIT — for contemporaneous interim marks; manipulation is inferred ex post from later unwinding
native_result: Some underperforming managers boost reported returns while fundraising, but they are less likely to raise a next fund; top-performing funds tend to understate valuations.
costs_capacity: Fund fees and illiquidity are embedded in LP outcomes, but allocator search costs and secondary-market execution are not modeled.
replication_decay: Consistent with evidence that interim NAVs are noisy and only moderately predict final performance; no independent Burgiss-data replication.
openness: Public NBER manuscript and verified DOI; Burgiss and StepStone data are proprietary.
key_limitation: Manipulation is inferred from performance paths rather than directly observed valuation intent, and selection into follow-on fundraising is endogenous.

authors: Robert S. Harris; Tim Jenkinson; Steven N. Kaplan; Ruediger Stucke
title: Has Persistence Persisted in Private Equity? Evidence from Buyout and Venture Capital Funds
geography_market: United States institutional buyout and venture funds
target: Next-fund PME, MOIC, and IRR persistence
horizon: H6: successive fund vintages over more than three decades
predictor_family: Interim prior-fund performance available at fundraising
model_family: Persistence regressions and performance-quartile transitions
sample_design: Burgiss institutional cash flows and NAVs through 2020-12, covering more than three decades; interim prior-fund performance is measured before the next fund's first capital call.
benchmark: Final or latest prior-fund performance versus information actually available at fundraising
pit_status: PIT — primary tests use interim performance available to LPs at fundraising
native_result: Buyout persistence weakens over time and is largely absent post-2000 at the decision date; VC persistence remains but also declines after 2000.
costs_capacity: Fund-level net performance is used; access constraints, commitment pacing, liquidity, and allocator portfolio capacity remain material.
replication_decay: Confirms Braun, Jenkinson, and Stoff's declining buyout persistence and revises the ex post Kaplan-Schoar interpretation while preserving a narrower VC claim.
openness: Public NBER and BFI manuscripts and verified DOI; Burgiss data are proprietary.
key_limitation: Interim marks are noisy and fundraising is endogenous; surviving VC persistence does not imply open access or scalable allocation.

authors: Gregory W. Brown; Éric Ghysels; Oleg R. Gredil
title: Nowcasting Net Asset Values: The Case of Private Equity
geography_market: Institutional buyout and venture funds in Burgiss
target: Weekly unsmoothed NAV, beta, and total risk
horizon: Contemporaneous weekly nowcast, not a forward return horizon
predictor_family: Reported NAVs, fund cash flows, and public comparable returns
model_family: Mixed-frequency state-space model and Kalman filtering
